title.zh: 卷九十九 列傳第四十九: 崔日用 張嘉貞 蕭嵩 張九齡 李適之 嚴挺之
title.en: Volume 99 Biographies 49: Cui Riyong, Zhang Jiazhen, Xiao Song, Zhang Jiuling, Li Shizhi, Yan Tingzhi
title.raw: 卷九十九 列傳第四十九: 崔日用 張嘉貞 蕭嵩 張九齡 李適之 嚴挺之 Volume 99 Biographies 49: Cui Riyong, Zhang Jiazhen, Xiao Song, Zhang Jiuling, Li Shizhi, Yan Tingzhi

sentences.zh: 崔日用

translations.literal: Cui Riyong
translations.idiomatic: Cui Riyong

sentences.zh: 神龍中，秘書監鄭普思納女後宮，潛謀左道，日用遽奏劾之。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era, Secretariat Director Zheng Pusi presented his daughter to the inner palace and secretly plotted heterodox practices; Riyong urgently memorialized impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong reign, when Secretariat Director Zheng Pusi sent his daughter into the inner palace and secretly pursued unorthodox rites, Cui Riyong at once memorialized to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 普思方承恩，中宗不之省。

translations.literal: Pusi was then enjoying imperial favor, and Emperor Zhongzong paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Pusi was then in high favor, and Emperor Zhongzong took no notice.

sentences.zh: 日用廷爭懇至，詞甚抗直，普思竟伏其罪。

translations.literal: Riyong argued strenuously at court with earnest, forthright language, and Pusi was made to confess his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Riyong disputed him earnestly at court in very blunt terms, and in the end Pusi admitted his guilt.

sentences.zh: 時宗楚客、武三思、武延秀等遞為朋黨，日用潛皆附之，驟遷兵部侍郎兼修文館學士。

translations.literal: At that time Zong Chuke, Wu Sansi, Wu Yanxiu and others formed factions in turn; Riyong secretly attached himself to them and was rapidly promoted to Vice Minister of War and Academician of the Xiuxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zong Chuke, Wu Sansi, Wu Yanxiu and others took turns as a faction; Riyong secretly joined them all and was suddenly promoted to Vice Minister of War and Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature.

sentences.zh: 中宗暴崩，韋庶人稱制，日用恐禍及己。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong died suddenly, Empress Wei assumed regency, and Riyong feared disaster would reach him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong died suddenly and Empress Wei seized power, Riyong feared calamity would overtake him.

sentences.zh: 知玄宗將圖義舉，乃因沙門普潤、道士王曄密詣籓邸，深自結納，潛謀翼戴。

translations.literal: Learning that Emperor Xuanzong was planning a righteous uprising, he went through the monk Purun and the Daoist Wang Ye to visit the prince's residence in secret, bonded with him deeply, and secretly plotted to support him.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Emperor Xuanzong was planning a righteous rising, he went by way of the monk Purun and the Daoist Wang Ye to the prince's residence in secret, bound himself closely to him, and secretly plotted to support his enthronement.

sentences.zh: 玄宗嘗謂曰：「今謀此舉，直為親，不為身。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong once said to him: "In this undertaking we pursue now, it is purely for our kin, not for ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once told him, "In plotting this action now, it is solely for kin, not for oneself.

sentences.zh: 日用曰：「此乃孝感動天，事必克捷。

translations.literal: Riyong said: "This is filial feeling that moves Heaven—the affair is sure to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Riyong said, "This is filial devotion that moves Heaven; the matter is certain to succeed.

sentences.zh: 望速發，出其不意，若少遲延，或恐生變。」

translations.literal: I beg you launch quickly and take them unawares; if you delay even slightly, I fear change may arise."
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will launch at once and catch them unprepared; if you delay even a little, I fear trouble may arise."

sentences.zh: 及討平韋氏，其夜，令權知雍州長史事。

translations.literal: When the Wei clan was suppressed, that very night he was ordered to act as Administrator of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei faction was put down, that same night he was ordered to serve provisionally as Administrator of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 以功授銀青光祿大夫、黃門侍郎，參知機務，封齊國公，食實封二百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate, participant in state affairs, enfeoffed Duke of Qi with an actual fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate, given a role in state affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, and granted an actual fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 為相月餘，與中書侍郎薛稷不協，於中書忿競，由是轉雍州長史，停知政事。

translations.literal: After more than a month as chief minister, he fell out with Vice Minister of the Secretariat Xue Ji and quarreled angrily at the Secretariat; he was therefore transferred to Administrator of Yongzhou and ceased participating in government.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as chief minister for a little over a month, he quarreled with Vice Minister of the Secretariat Xue Ji at the Secretariat; he was therefore made Administrator of Yongzhou and ceased handling state affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋出為揚州長史，歷婺、汴二州刺史、兗州都督、荊州長史。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as Administrator of Yangzhou, and served successively as Governor of Wu and Bian prefectures, Military Commissioner of Yanzhou, and Administrator of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was posted out as Administrator of Yangzhou, then served in turn as Governor of Wu and Bian, Military Commissioner of Yanzhou, and Administrator of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 因入奏事，言：「太平公主謀逆有期，陛下往在宮府，欲有討捕，猶是子道臣道，須用謀用力。

translations.literal: On entering to report affairs he said: "Princess Taiping's rebellion is due; when Your Majesty was still in the palace residence and wished to seize and suppress her, it was still the way of son and subject—you had to use stratagem and force.
translations.idiomatic: When he came in to report on affairs he said, "Princess Taiping's plot to rebel is imminent. When Your Majesty was still in the palace residence and wished to seize and suppress her, that was still the way of son and subject—you had to use stratagem and force.

sentences.zh: 今既光臨大寶，但須下一制，誰敢不從？

translations.literal: Now that you have ascended the Great Treasure, you need only issue one edict—who would dare disobey?
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have taken the throne, you need only issue one edict—who would dare not obey?

sentences.zh: 忽奸宄得志，則禍亂不小。」

translations.literal: If traitors suddenly gain their wish, the calamity and disorder will be no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: If traitors suddenly get their way, the harm and turmoil will be considerable.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「誠如此，直恐驚動太上皇，卿宜更思之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "If it is truly so, I fear only that the Retired Emperor would be alarmed; you should think further."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "If that is truly so, I fear only alarming the Retired Emperor; you should reconsider."

sentences.zh: 日用曰：「臣聞天子孝與庶人孝全別。

translations.literal: Riyong said: "I have heard that the Son of Heaven's filial piety and the commoner's filial piety are wholly different.
translations.idiomatic: Riyong said, "I have heard that the Son of Heaven's filial piety and the common people's filial piety are completely different.

sentences.zh: 庶人孝，謹身節用，承順顏色；

translations.literal: Commoner's filial piety is to keep the body disciplined and expenditures restrained and to comply with one's parents' countenance;
translations.idiomatic: The common people's filial piety is to keep the person disciplined and spending restrained and to defer to their parents' wishes;

sentences.zh: 天子孝，安國家，定社稷。

translations.literal: the Son of Heaven's filial piety is to secure the state and settle the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: the Son of Heaven's filial piety is to secure the state and settle the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 今若逆黨竊發，即大業都棄，豈得成天子之孝乎！

translations.literal: If the rebel faction steals forth now, the great enterprise will all be abandoned—how could that fulfill the Son of Heaven's filial piety!
translations.idiomatic: If the rebel faction rises now, the great enterprise will all be cast away—how could that fulfill the Son of Heaven's filial piety!

sentences.zh: 伏請先定北軍，次收逆黨，即不驚動太上皇。」

translations.literal: I beg first to secure the Northern Army, next to seize the rebel faction—then the Retired Emperor will not be alarmed."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that you first secure the Northern Army, then seize the rebel faction—the Retired Emperor will then not be alarmed."

sentences.zh: 玄宗從其議。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor adopted his plan.

sentences.zh: 及討蕭至忠、竇懷貞之際，又令權檢校雍州長史，加實封通前滿四百戶。

translations.literal: When Xiao Zhibo and Dou Huaizhen were suppressed, he was again ordered to serve provisionally as Inspector-General of Yongzhou, and his actual fief was increased to four hundred households in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Zhibo and Dou Huaizhen were suppressed, he was again ordered to serve provisionally as Inspector-General of Yongzhou, and his actual fief was increased to a total of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 日用嘗采《毛詩》、《大雅》、《小雅》二十篇及司馬相如《封禪書》，因上生日表上之，以申規諷，並述告成之事。

translations.literal: Riyong once selected twenty pieces from the Mao Odes, the Greater and Lesser Elegantiae, and Sima Xiangru's "Feng and Shan Sacrifice" and presented them on a birthday memorial to offer admonition and also to describe the matter of announcing completion.
translations.idiomatic: Riyong once culled twenty pieces from the Mao Odes, the Greater and Lesser Elegantiae, and Sima Xiangru's "Feng and Shan Sacrifice" and, on a birthday memorial, presented them to offer admonition and also to describe the matter of announcing completion.

sentences.zh: 手詔答曰：「夫詩者，動天地，感鬼神，厚於人，美於教矣。

translations.literal: The imperial handwritten reply said: "Poetry moves Heaven and earth, touches spirits and ghosts, is generous to people, and is beautiful in teaching.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's handwritten reply said, "Poetry moves Heaven and earth, touches spirits and ghosts, is generous toward people, and is beautiful in teaching.

sentences.zh: 朕志之所尚，思與之齊，庶乎采詩之官，補朕之闕。

translations.literal: What my will esteems, I wish to align with it, so that perhaps the officers who gather poems may supply my lacks.
translations.idiomatic: What my will esteems, I wish to align with it, so that perhaps the officers who gather poems may supply what I lack.

sentences.zh: 且古者封禪，升中告成，朕以菲德，未明於至道。

translations.literal: Moreover, in antiquity the feng and shan sacrifices ascended the central peak to announce completion; with my slight virtue I am not clear on the utmost Way.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in antiquity the feng and shan sacrifices ascended the central peak to announce completion; with my slight virtue I am not clear on the utmost Way.

sentences.zh: 竦然以聽，頗壯相如之詞；

translations.literal: Startled, I listened and was quite heartened by Xiangru's words;
translations.idiomatic: Startled, I listened and was quite heartened by Xiangru's words;

sentences.zh: 惕然載懷，復慚夷吾之語。

translations.literal: wary, I bore it in mind and again felt ashamed at Guan Zhong's words.
translations.idiomatic: wary, I bore it in mind and again felt ashamed at Guan Zhong's words.

sentences.zh: 卿洽聞殫見，溫故知新，逮此發揮，益彰忠懇。

translations.literal: You are broadly informed and exhaustively perceptive, warm the old to know the new; in reaching this expression you further display loyal earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: You are broadly informed and exhaustively perceptive, warm the old to know the new; in reaching this expression you further display loyal earnestness.

sentences.zh: 豈非討蓬山之籍，心不忘於起予；

translations.literal: Is it not that in searching the registers of Mount Peng you do not forget to rouse me;
translations.idiomatic: Is it not that in searching the registers of Mount Peng your heart does not forget to rouse me;

sentences.zh: 因蘭殿之祥，言固深於啟沃，朕循環覽諷，用慰於懷。

translations.literal: through the auspice of the Orchid Hall your words are indeed deep in counsel; I read them round and round to comfort my heart.
translations.idiomatic: through the auspice of the Orchid Hall your words are indeed deep in counsel; I read them round and round to comfort my heart.

sentences.zh: 今賜卿衣裳一副、物五十段，以示無言不酬之信也。」

translations.literal: Now I grant you one set of garments and fifty lengths of goods, to show the faith that no word goes unrewarded."
translations.idiomatic: Now I grant you one set of garments and fifty lengths of goods, to show the faith that no word goes unrewarded."

sentences.zh: 尋出為常州刺史，削實封三百戶，轉汝州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as Governor of Changzhou, his actual fief was reduced by three hundred households, and he was transferred to Governor of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as Governor of Changzhou, his actual fief was cut by three hundred households, and he was transferred to Governor of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 開元七年，差降口賦，特下敕曰：「唐元之際，逆黨構凶，崔日用當時潛論其事，及於戡翦，實預元謀，而所食之封，後以例減。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaiyuan, when corvée levies were reduced by decree, a special edict said: "At the time of the Restoration of Tang, the rebel faction plotted harm; Cui Riyong at the time secretly discussed the matter and, when it was suppressed, truly took part in the original plot, yet the fief he received was later reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kaiyuan, when corvée levies were reduced by decree, a special edict said, "At the time of the Restoration of Tang, the rebel faction plotted harm; Cui Riyong at the time secretly discussed the matter and, when it was suppressed, truly took part in the original plot, yet the fief he received was later reduced by precedent.

sentences.zh: 功既居多，特宜準初食之封，與二百戶。」

translations.literal: His merit was especially great; it is fitting that his fief be restored to the original grant of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was especially great; it is fitting that his fief be restored to the original grant of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十年，轉并州大都督長史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Chief Administrator of the Metropolitan Area of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to Chief Administrator of the Metropolitan Area of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，時年五十，贈吏部尚書，謚曰昭。

translations.literal: Soon he died, aged fifty; he was posthumously made Minister of Personnel, with the posthumous title Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died at the age of fifty; he was posthumously made Minister of Personnel, with the posthumous title Zhao.

sentences.zh: 後又贈荊州大都督，子宗之襲。

translations.literal: Later he was again posthumously made Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhou; his son Zongzhi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was again posthumously made Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhou; his son Zongzhi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 日用才辯過人，見事敏速，每朝廷有事，轉禍為福，以取富貴。

translations.literal: Riyong's talent and eloquence surpassed others; he saw affairs swiftly; whenever the court had trouble he turned calamity into fortune to gain wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Riyong's talent and eloquence surpassed others and he saw affairs swiftly; whenever the court had trouble he turned calamity into fortune to gain wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 及先天已後，復求入相，竟亦不遂。

translations.literal: After the Xiantian era he again sought to enter the chancellorship but in the end did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xiantian era he again sought to become chief minister but in the end did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 常謂人曰：「吾一生行事，皆臨時制變，不必重專守始謀。

translations.literal: He often told people: "In all my life's actions I adapt on the spot; one need not cling heavily to the original plan.
translations.idiomatic: He often told people, "In all my life's actions I adapt on the spot; one need not cling heavily to the original plan.

sentences.zh: 每一念之，不覺芒刺在於背也。」

translations.literal: Each time I think of it, I cannot help feeling bristles on my back."
translations.idiomatic: Each time I think of it, I cannot help feeling bristles on my back."

sentences.zh: 崔日知

translations.literal: Cui Rizhi
translations.idiomatic: Cui Rizhi

sentences.zh: 日用從父兄日知，亦有吏幹。

translations.literal: Riyong's elder cousin by the same clan, Rizhi, also had administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: Riyong's elder cousin by the same clan, Rizhi, also had administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 景雲中為洛州司馬。

translations.literal: In the Jingyun era he was Vice Magistrate of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingyun era he served as Vice Magistrate of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 會譙王重福入東都作亂，群臣皆避難逃匿，日知獨督率人吏赴留守，與屯營合勢討賊。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qiao Li Chongfu entered the Eastern Capital to rebel, the ministers all fled and hid; Rizhi alone led clerks and staff to the garrison commander and joined camp forces to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Qiao Li Chongfu entered the Eastern Capital to rebel, the ministers all fled and hid; Rizhi alone led clerks and staff to the garrison commander and joined camp forces to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 重福既死，以功加銀青光祿大夫，累遷京兆尹。

translations.literal: After Chongfu died, for his merit he was promoted to Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and rose in succession to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongfu died, for his merit he was promoted to Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and rose in succession to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 坐贓為御史李如璧所劾，左遷歙縣丞，俄又歷遷殿中監。

translations.literal: For corruption he was impeached by Censor Li Rubi, demoted to Assistant Magistrate of She County, and soon rose again in succession to Director of the Palace Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: For corruption he was impeached by Censor Li Rubi, demoted to Assistant Magistrate of She County, and soon rose again in succession to Director of the Palace Directorate.

sentences.zh: 日知素與張說友善，說薦之，奏請授御史大夫，上不許。

translations.literal: Rizhi had long been friendly with Zhang Yue; Yue recommended him and memorialized to appoint him Censor-in-Chief, but the Emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Rizhi had long been friendly with Zhang Yue; Yue recommended him and memorialized to appoint him Censor-in-Chief, but the Emperor did not consent.

sentences.zh: 遂以為左羽林懷大將軍，而以河南尹崔隱甫為御史大夫，隱甫由是與說不葉。

translations.literal: He was therefore made General of the Left Feathered Forest Guard, while Metropolitan Governor of Henan Cui Yinpu was made Censor-in-Chief; Yinpu therefore fell out with Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore made General of the Left Feathered Forest Guard, while Metropolitan Governor of Henan Cui Yinpu was made Censor-in-Chief; Yinpu therefore fell out with Yue.

sentences.zh: 日知俄遷太常卿。

translations.literal: Rizhi was soon transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Rizhi was soon transferred to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 自以歷任年久，每朝士參集，常與尚書同列，時人號為「尚書裏行」，遂為口實。

translations.literal: Considering that he had served many years, whenever courtiers assembled he was regularly ranked with the Ministers; people of the time called him "the Minister in practice," and it became a byword.
translations.idiomatic: Considering that he had served many years, whenever courtiers assembled he was regularly ranked with the Ministers; people of the time called him "the Minister in practice," and it became a byword.

sentences.zh: 開元十六年，出為潞州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan he was sent out as Chief Administrator of the Metropolitan Area of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan he was sent out as Chief Administrator of the Metropolitan Area of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋以年老致仕，卒，謚曰襄。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of age, he retired; he died, with the posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on account of age, he retired from office; he died, with the posthumous title Xiang.

sentences.zh: 張嘉貞

translations.literal: Zhang Jiazhen
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiazhen

sentences.zh: 張嘉貞，蒲州猗氏人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiazhen was a man of Yishi in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiazhen was a native of Yishi in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弱冠應五經舉，拜平鄉尉，坐事免歸鄉里。

translations.literal: At twenty he answered the Five Classics examination, was appointed Vice Magistrate of Pingxiang, and was dismissed and returned home for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he answered the Five Classics examination, was appointed Vice Magistrate of Pingxiang, and was dismissed and returned home for an offense.

sentences.zh: 長安中，侍御史張循憲為河東采訪使，薦嘉貞材堪憲官，請以己之官秩授之。

translations.literal: In the Chang'an era, Investigating Censor Zhang Xunxian was Commissioner for the Hedong Circuit and recommended Jiazhen as fit for a censorial post, asking to transfer his own rank to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chang'an era, Investigating Censor Zhang Xunxian was Commissioner for the Hedong Circuit and recommended Jiazhen as fit for a censorial post, asking to transfer his own rank to him.

sentences.zh: 則天召見，垂簾與之言，嘉貞奏曰：「以臣草萊而得入謁九重，是千載一遇也。

translations.literal: Empress Wu summoned him and, with the curtain lowered, spoke with him; Jiazhen memorialized: "That I, a man of the wilds, may enter audience in the Ninefold Palace is a meeting once in a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu summoned him and, with the curtain lowered, spoke with him; Jiazhen memorialized, "That I, a man of the wilds, may enter audience in the Ninefold Palace is a meeting once in a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 咫尺之間，如隔雲務，竟不睹日月，恐君臣之道有所未盡。」

translations.literal: Within a foot's distance it is as if separated by clouds and mist; I cannot see sun and moon after all—I fear the way of ruler and subject is not fully fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Within a foot's distance it is as if separated by clouds and mist; I cannot see sun and moon after all—I fear the way of ruler and subject is not fully fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 則天遽令卷簾，與語大悅，擢拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Empress Wu at once ordered the curtain rolled up; she spoke with him with great delight and promoted him Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu at once ordered the curtain rolled up; she spoke with him with great delight and promoted him Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書舍人，歷秦州都督、并州長史，為政嚴肅，甚為人吏所畏。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat, served as Military Commissioner of Qinzhou and Chief Administrator of Bingzhou, and in governing was stern and severe, greatly feared by clerks and staff.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat, served as Military Commissioner of Qinzhou and Chief Administrator of Bingzhou, and in governing was stern and severe, greatly feared by clerks and staff.

sentences.zh: 開元初，因奏事至京師，上聞其善政，數加賞慰。

translations.literal: In early Kaiyuan, when he came to the capital to report on affairs, the Emperor heard of his good government and repeatedly added praise and consolation.
translations.idiomatic: In early Kaiyuan, when he came to the capital to report on affairs, the Emperor heard of his good government and repeatedly added praise and consolation.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞因奏曰：「臣少孤，兄弟相依以至今。

translations.literal: Jiazhen therefore memorialized: "I was orphaned young; my brothers have relied on one another until now.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen therefore memorialized, "I was orphaned young; my brothers have relied on one another until now.

sentences.zh: 臣弟嘉祐，今授鄯州別駕，與臣各在一方，同心離居，魂絕萬里。

translations.literal: My younger brother Jiayou is now appointed Vice Prefect of Binzhou; he and I are each in a different region—of one heart but living apart, our souls are severed by ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: My younger brother Jiayou is now appointed Vice Prefect of Binzhou; he and I are each in a different region—of one heart but living apart, our souls are severed by ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 乞移就臣側近，臣兄弟盡力報國，死無所恨。」

translations.literal: I beg that he be moved near me; my brothers will do our utmost to repay the state and will die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that he be moved near me; my brothers will do our utmost to repay the state and will die without regret.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其友愛，特改嘉祐為忻州刺史。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised their brotherly affection and specially changed Jiayou to Governor of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised their brotherly affection and specially changed Jiayou to Governor of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 時突厥九姓新來內附，散居太原以北，嘉貞奏請置軍以鎮之，於是始於并州置天兵軍，以嘉貞為使。

translations.literal: At the time the nine surnames of the Turks had newly submitted and were scattered north of Taiyuan; Jiazhen memorialized to establish an army to garrison them, and so the Heavenly Troops Army was first established at Bingzhou, with Jiazhen as its commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the nine surnames of the Turks had newly submitted and were scattered north of Taiyuan; Jiazhen memorialized to establish an army to garrison them, and so the Heavenly Troops Army was first established at Bingzhou, with Jiazhen as its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六年春，嘉貞又入朝。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year Jiazhen again entered court.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year Jiazhen again entered court.

sentences.zh: 俄有告其在軍奢僭及贓賄者，御史大夫王晙因而劾奏之，按驗無狀，上將加告者反坐之罪。

translations.literal: Soon someone reported that in the army he was extravagant and had taken bribes; Censor-in-Chief Wang Jun therefore impeached him; investigation found no basis, and the Emperor was about to punish the accuser with counter-charge.
translations.idiomatic: Soon someone reported that in the army he was extravagant and had taken bribes; Censor-in-Chief Wang Jun therefore impeached him; investigation found no basis, and the Emperor was about to punish the accuser with counter-charge.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞奏曰：「昔者天子聽政於上，瞍賦矇誦，百工諫，庶人謗，而後天子斟酌焉。

translations.literal: Jiazhen memorialized: "In antiquity the Son of Heaven heard government above; the blind recited and the sightless chanted, the hundred craftsmen remonstrated, and the common people criticized—only then did the Son of Heaven weigh it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen memorialized, "In antiquity the Son of Heaven heard government above; the blind recited and the sightless chanted, the hundred craftsmen remonstrated, and the common people criticized—only then did the Son of Heaven weigh it.

sentences.zh: 今反坐此輩，是塞言者之路，則天下之事無由上達。

translations.literal: To counter-charge these men now is to block the road of those who speak, and then affairs under Heaven cannot reach above.
translations.idiomatic: To counter-charge these men now is to block the road of those who speak, and then affairs under Heaven cannot reach above.

sentences.zh: 特望免此罪，以廣謗誦之道。」

translations.literal: I especially beg to waive this punishment, to broaden the way of criticism and recitation.
translations.idiomatic: I especially beg to waive this punishment, to broaden the way of criticism and recitation.

sentences.zh: 從之，遂令減死，自是帝以嘉貞為忠。

translations.literal: The Emperor consented and ordered the death penalty reduced; from this the Emperor regarded Jiazhen as loyal.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor consented and ordered the death penalty reduced; from this the Emperor regarded Jiazhen as loyal.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞又嘗奏曰：「今誌力方壯，是效命之秋，更三數年，即衰老無能為也。

translations.literal: Jiazhen also once memorialized: "Now my will and strength are in their prime—it is the season to devote my life; in another few years I will be old and feeble and unable to act.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen also once memorialized, "Now my will and strength are in their prime—it is the season to devote my life; in another few years I will be old and feeble and unable to act.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下早垂任使，死且不憚。」

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty early bestows employment, I will not fear death.
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Majesty early bestows employment, I will not fear death.

sentences.zh: 上以其明辯，尤重之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because of his clarity in argument, especially valued him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, because of his clarity in argument, especially valued him.

sentences.zh: 八年春，宋璟、蘇颋罷知政事，擢嘉貞為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year Song Jing and Su Ting ceased handling government affairs; Jiazhen was promoted Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year Song Jing and Su Ting ceased handling government affairs; Jiazhen was promoted Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 數月，加銀青光祿大夫，遷中書令。

translations.literal: Several months later he was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and transferred to Chief Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and transferred to Chief Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞斷決敏速，善於敷奏，然性強躁自用，頗為時論所譏。

translations.literal: Jiazhen decided swiftly and was skilled at presenting memorials, yet by nature he was forceful, impatient, and self-willed, and was rather ridiculed in contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen decided swiftly and was skilled at presenting memorials, yet by nature he was forceful, impatient, and self-willed, and was rather ridiculed in contemporary opinion.

sentences.zh: 時中書舍人苗延嗣、呂太一、考功員外郎員嘉靜、殿中侍御史崔訓，皆嘉貞所引，位列清要，常在嘉貞門下共議朝政，時人為之語曰：「令公四俊，苗、呂、崔、員。」

translations.literal: At the time Drafting Attendant Miao Yansi, Lü Taiyi, Evaluation Section Vice Director Yuan Jiajing, and Palace Investigation Censor Cui Xun were all introduced by Jiazhen, held clear and important posts, and were constantly at Jiazhen's door discussing court government; people of the time made a saying: "The Chief Minister's four talents: Miao, Lü, Cui, Yuan."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Drafting Attendant Miao Yansi, Lü Taiyi, Evaluation Section Vice Director Yuan Jiajing, and Palace Investigation Censor Cui Xun were all introduced by Jiazhen, held clear and important posts, and were constantly at Jiazhen's door discussing court government; people of the time made a saying: "The Chief Minister's four talents: Miao, Lü, Cui, Yuan."

sentences.zh: 開元十年，車駕幸東都。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan the imperial carriage visited the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan the imperial carriage visited the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 有洛陽主簿王鈞為嘉貞修宅，將以求御史，因受贓事發，上特令朝堂集眾決殺之。

translations.literal: The Luoyang Registrar Wang Jun built a residence for Jiazhen intending to seek the post of censor; when the bribery affair broke out, the Emperor specially ordered him executed by collective decision in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Luoyang Registrar Wang Jun built a residence for Jiazhen intending to seek the post of censor; when the bribery affair broke out, the Emperor specially ordered him executed by collective decision in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞促所由速其刑以滅口，乃歸罪於御史大夫韋抗、中丞韋虛心，皆貶黜之。

translations.literal: Jiazhen urged the responsible officials to hurry the punishment to silence him, then blamed Censor-in-Chief Wei Kang and Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Xuxin, who were all demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen urged the responsible officials to hurry the punishment to silence him, then blamed Censor-in-Chief Wei Kang and Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Xuxin, who were all demoted.

sentences.zh: 其冬，秘書監姜皎犯罪，嘉貞又附會王守一奏請杖之，皎遂死於路。

translations.literal: That winter Secretariat Director Jiang Jiao committed an offense; Jiazhen again joined Wang Shouyi in memorializing to request beating with the staff, and Jiao died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Secretariat Director Jiang Jiao committed an offense; Jiazhen again joined Wang Shouyi in memorializing to request beating with the staff, and Jiao died on the road.

sentences.zh: 俄而廣州都督裴伷先下獄，上召侍臣問當何罪，嘉貞又請杖之。

translations.literal: Soon Military Commissioner of Guangzhou Pei Xianxian was imprisoned; the Emperor summoned attendants to ask what punishment was fitting, and Jiazhen again requested beating with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Military Commissioner of Guangzhou Pei Xianxian was imprisoned; the Emperor summoned attendants to ask what punishment was fitting, and Jiazhen again requested beating with the staff.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書張說進曰：「臣聞刑不上大夫，以其近於君也。

translations.literal: Minister of War Zhang Yue advanced and said: "I have heard that punishment does not reach the grand masters, because they are close to the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Zhang Yue advanced and said, "I have heard that punishment does not reach the grand masters, because they are close to the ruler.

sentences.zh: 故曰：『士可殺，不可辱。』

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: 'A gentleman may be killed but may not be insulted.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said, 'A gentleman may be killed but may not be insulted.

sentences.zh: 臣今秋受詔巡邊，中途聞姜皎以罪於朝堂決杖，配流而死。

translations.literal: This autumn I received orders to tour the border; midway I heard that Jiang Jiao, for his crime, was beaten with the staff in the court hall and died on assignment to exile.
translations.idiomatic: This autumn I received orders to tour the border; midway I heard that Jiang Jiao, for his crime, was beaten with the staff in the court hall and died on assignment to exile.

sentences.zh: 皎官是三品，亦有微功。

translations.literal: Jiao's office was third rank and he also had slight merit.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's office was third rank and he also had slight merit.

sentences.zh: 若其有犯，應死即殺，應流即流，不宜決杖廷辱，以卒伍待之。

translations.literal: If he had an offense, if death was fitting then kill him, if exile was fitting then exile him—he should not have been beaten with the staff and humiliated in court, treated like a common soldier.
translations.idiomatic: If he had an offense, if death was fitting then kill him, if exile was fitting then exile him—he should not have been beaten with the staff and humiliated in court, treated like a common soldier.

sentences.zh: 且律有八議，勛貴在焉。

translations.literal: Moreover the law has the Eight Deliberations; merit and nobility are among them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the law has the Eight Deliberations; merit and nobility are among them.

sentences.zh: 皎事已往，不可追悔。

translations.literal: Jiao's affair is already past and cannot be regretted.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's affair is already past and cannot be regretted.

sentences.zh: 伷先只宜據狀流貶，不可輕又決罰。」

translations.literal: Xianxian should only be exiled according to the facts; he should not lightly again be punished by beating.
translations.idiomatic: Xianxian should only be exiled according to the facts; he should not lightly again be punished by beating.

sentences.zh: 上然其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved his words.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞不悅，退謂說曰：「何言事之深也？」

translations.literal: Jiazhen was displeased; retiring he said to Yue: "Why speak on the affair so deeply?
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen was displeased; retiring he said to Yue, "Why speak on the affair so deeply?

sentences.zh: 說曰：「宰相者，時來即為，豈能長據？

translations.literal: Yue said: "A chief minister comes when the time comes—how can one hold the post long?
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "A chief minister takes office when the time arrives—who can hold the post for long?

sentences.zh: 若貴臣盡當可杖，但恐吾等行當及之。

translations.literal: If every noble minister ought to be beaten with the staff, I fear we too will soon reach that.
translations.idiomatic: If every noble minister ought to be beaten with the staff, I fear we too will soon come to the same.

sentences.zh: 此言非為伷先，乃為天下士君子也。」

translations.literal: These words are not for Xianxian alone but for gentlemen and scholars under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: I speak thus not for Xianxian alone but for gentlemen and scholars throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 初，嘉貞為兵部員外郎，時張說為侍郎。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jiazhen was Vice Director in the Ministry of War, Zhang Yue was Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Jiazhen was Vice Director in the Ministry of War, Zhang Yue was Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 及是，說位在嘉貞下，既無所推讓，說頗不平，因以此言激怒嘉貞，由是與說不葉。

translations.literal: By this time Yue's rank was below Jiazhen's; since he made no deferential gesture, Yue was quite discontent and used these words to provoke Jiazhen, and from this he fell out with Yue.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yue stood below Jiazhen yet offered no deference; displeased, he used these words to provoke him, and the two fell out.

sentences.zh: 上又以嘉貞弟嘉祐為金吾將軍，兄弟並居將相之位，甚為時人之所畏憚。

translations.literal: The Emperor also made Jiazhen's younger brother Jiayou General of the Golden Guards; the brothers together held ministerial and general rank, greatly feared by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also appointed Jiazhen's younger brother Jiayou General of the Golden Guards; with both brothers in ministerial and military posts, contemporaries greatly feared them.

sentences.zh: 十一年，上幸太原行在所，嘉祐贓汙事發。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Emperor visited the Taiyuan traveling palace; Jiayou's corruption affair broke out.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when the Emperor visited the Taiyuan traveling palace, Jiayou's corruption came to light.

sentences.zh: 張說勸嘉貞素服待罪，不得入謁，因出為幽州刺史，說遂代為中書令。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue urged Jiazhen to wear plain garments and await punishment, not to enter audience; he was therefore sent out as Governor of Youzhou, and Yue then replaced him as Chief Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue urged Jiazhen to wear plain garments and await punishment and not enter audience; he was sent out as Governor of Youzhou, and Yue replaced him as Chief Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞惋恨，謂人曰：「中書令幸有二員，何相迫之甚也！」

translations.literal: Jiazhen was resentful and told people: "Fortunate that there can be two Chief Ministers of the Secretariat—why press me so hard!
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen brooded and said, "The Secretariat may have two chiefs—why press me so hard?

sentences.zh: 明年，復拜戶部尚書，兼益州長史，判都督事。

translations.literal: The next year he was again appointed Minister of Revenue and concurrently Chief Administrator of Yizhou, with authority over military affairs as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was again made Minister of Revenue and concurrently Chief Administrator of Yizhou, with authority over military affairs.

sentences.zh: 敕嘉貞就中書省與宰相會宴，嘉貞既恨張說擠己，因攘袂勃罵，源乾曜、王晙共和解之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jiazhen to banquet with the chief ministers at the Secretariat; Jiazhen, hating Zhang Yue for squeezing him out, rolled up his sleeves and reviled him fiercely; Yuan Qianyao and Wang Jun together pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to banquet with the chief ministers at the Secretariat, Jiazhen—hating Zhang Yue for forcing him out—rolled up his sleeves and reviled him; Yuan Qianyao and Wang Jun together restrained them.

sentences.zh: 明年，坐與王守一交往，左轉臺州刺史。

translations.literal: The next year, for associating with Wang Shouyi, he was demoted to Governor of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, for associating with Wang Shouyi, he was demoted to Governor of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 復代盧從願為工部尚書、定州刺史，知北平軍事，累封河東侯。

translations.literal: He again replaced Lu Congyuan as Minister of Works and Governor of Dingzhou, with command of Pingbei military affairs, and was enfeoffed in succession as Marquis of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He again replaced Lu Congyuan as Minister of Works and Governor of Dingzhou, commanding Pingbei military affairs, and was enfeoffed in succession as Marquis of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 將行，上自賦詩，詔百僚於上東門外餞之。

translations.literal: When he was about to depart, the Emperor himself composed a poem and ordered the hundred officials to see him off outside the Upper East Gate.
translations.idiomatic: As he was to depart, the Emperor composed a poem himself and ordered the hundred officials to see him off outside the Upper East Gate.

sentences.zh: 至州，於恆嶽廟中立頌，嘉貞自為其文，乃書於石，其碑用白石為之，素質黑文，甚為奇麗。

translations.literal: At the prefecture he erected a eulogy stele in the Mount Heng temple, wrote the text himself, and had it carved on stone; the stele was of white stone with plain quality and black inscription, very strange and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: At the prefecture he set up a eulogy in the Mount Heng temple, wrote the text himself, and inscribed it on stone; the stele was white stone with black characters, strikingly beautiful.

sentences.zh: 先是，嶽祠為遠近祈賽，有錢數百萬，嘉貞自以為頌文之功，納其數萬。

translations.literal: Before this the mountain shrine had been used for prayers near and far, with several million in cash; Jiazhen, considering it the merit of his eulogy text, took several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The shrine had long drawn prayers from far and near, with cash in the millions; Jiazhen, claiming merit for his eulogy, took several tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 十七年，嘉貞以疾請就醫東都，制從之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Jiazhen, ill, requested to seek treatment in the Eastern Capital; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Jiazhen, ill, asked to seek treatment in the Eastern Capital; an edict granted his request.

sentences.zh: 至都，目瞑無所見，上令醫人內直郎田休裕、郎將呂弘泰馳傳往省療之。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital his eyes were closed and he could see nothing; the Emperor sent the inner-attending physician Tian Xiuyu and the commandant Lü Hongtai by rapid relay to examine and treat him.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital his eyes were shut and he could see nothing; the Emperor sent the inner-attending physician Tian Xiuyu and Commandant Lü Hongtai by rapid relay to treat him.

sentences.zh: 其秋卒，年六十四，贈益州大都督。

translations.literal: That autumn he died, aged sixty-four; he was posthumously made Metropolitan Governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he died at sixty-four; he was posthumously made Metropolitan Governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 謚曰恭肅。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Gongsu.
translations.idiomatic: He received the posthumous title Gongsu.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞雖久歷清要，然不立田園。

translations.literal: Although Jiazhen had long held clear and important posts, he did not establish estates.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jiazhen had long held eminent posts, he established no private estates.

sentences.zh: 及在定州，所親有勸植田業者，嘉貞曰：「吾忝歷官榮，曾任國相，未死之際，豈憂饑餒？

translations.literal: When he was at Dingzhou, those close to him urged planting fields; Jiazhen said: "I have disgraced myself by holding honorable office and once served as state chief minister; before I die, why worry about hunger?
translations.idiomatic: At Dingzhou, intimates urged him to plant estates; Jiazhen said, "I have enjoyed honorable rank and once served as chief minister; before death, why fear hunger?

sentences.zh: 若負譴責，雖富田莊，亦無用也。

translations.literal: If I bear censure and punishment, even rich fields and manors are of no use.
translations.idiomatic: If I bear censure, even vast estates are useless.

sentences.zh: 比見朝士廣占良田，及身沒後，皆為無賴子弟作酒色之資，甚無謂也。」

translations.literal: I have seen court gentlemen widely seize good fields; after they die, all become resources for worthless younger kin for wine and women—very pointless.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen courtiers seize broad estates; after death their worthless sons use them only for wine and women—utterly pointless.

sentences.zh: 聞者皆嘆伏。

translations.literal: Hearers all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard him sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 初，嘉貞作相，薦萬年縣主簿韓朝宗，擢為監察御史。

translations.literal: When Jiazhen first became chief minister he recommended Han Chaozong, Registrar of Wannian County, and promoted him Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiazhen first became chief minister he recommended Han Chaozong, Registrar of Wannian County, and made him Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 及嘉貞卒後十數歲，朝宗為京兆尹，因奏曰：「自陛下臨御已來，所用宰相，皆進退以禮，善始令終，身雖已沒，子孫咸在朝廷。

translations.literal: More than ten years after Jiazhen died, Chaozong as Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao memorialized: "Since Your Majesty took the throne, every chief minister you have used has advanced and retired by ritual, beginning well and ending well; though dead, their descendants all remain at court.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years after Jiazhen's death, Chaozong as Metropolitan Governor memorialized, "Since Your Majesty began to rule, every chief minister has advanced and retired with propriety; though dead, their sons and grandsons remain at court.

sentences.zh: 唯張嘉貞晚年一子，今猶未登官序。」

translations.literal: Only Zhang Jiazhen in his later years had one son who still has not entered the official sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhang Jiazhen, in his later years, had one son who still has not entered office.

sentences.zh: 上亦惘然，遽令召之，賜名延賞，特拜左內率府兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor too was moved; he at once ordered him summoned, granted the name Yanbao, and specially appointed him Army Adjutant of the Left Inner Rate Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor too was moved; he at once summoned the son, granted the name Yanbao, and specially appointed him Army Adjutant of the Left Inner Rate Office.

sentences.zh: 德宗朝，位至宰輔，自有傳。

translations.literal: In the Dezong reign he reached the chancellorship; he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Dezong he reached the chancellorship; he has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 張嘉祐

translations.literal: Zhang Jiayou
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiayou

sentences.zh: 嘉祐，有幹略，自右金吾將軍貶浦陽府折沖，至二十五年，為相州刺史。

translations.literal: Jiayou had ability and plan; from General of the Right Golden Guards he was demoted to Colonel of Puyang Prefecture; by the twenty-fifth year he was Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou was capable and resourceful; demoted from General of the Right Golden Guards to Colonel of Puyang, by the twenty-fifth year he was Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 相州自開元已來，刺史死貶者十數人，嘉祐訪知尉遲迥周末為相州總管，身死國難，乃立其神祠以邀福。

translations.literal: Since Kaiyuan, ten-odd governors of Xiangzhou had died or been demoted; Jiayou learned that at the end of the Northern Zhou Yuwen Jiong had been Metropolitan Commander of Xiangzhou and died for the state, and therefore erected his spirit shrine to seek blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Since Kaiyuan, a dozen governors of Xiangzhou had died or been demoted; Jiayou learned that Yuwen Jiong had died for the state as commander there and erected his shrine to seek blessing.

sentences.zh: 經三考，改左金吾將軍。

translations.literal: After three evaluations he was made General of the Left Golden Guards.
translations.idiomatic: After three evaluations he was made General of the Left Golden Guards.

sentences.zh: 後吳兢為鄴郡守，又加尉遲神冕服。

translations.literal: Later Wu Jing as Administrator of Ye Prefecture again added ceremonial cap and robes to the Yuwen spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wu Jing governed Ye Prefecture, he again added ceremonial cap and robes to the Yuwen spirit.

sentences.zh: 自後郡守無患。

translations.literal: After that prefectural governors had no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter prefectural governors suffered no ill fortune.

sentences.zh: 蕭嵩，貞觀初左僕射、宋國公瑀之曾侄孫。

translations.literal: Xiao Song was the great-grandnephew of Xiao Yu, Left Vice Director and Duke of Song, in early Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Song was the great-grandnephew of Xiao Yu, Left Vice Director and Duke of Song, in early Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 祖鈞，中書舍人，有名於時。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jun was Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat, famous in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jun was Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat and famed in his day.

sentences.zh: 嵩美須髯，儀形偉麗。

translations.literal: Song had a beautiful beard and a grand, imposing appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Song had a fine beard and a grand, imposing bearing.

sentences.zh: 初，娶會稽賀晦女，與吳郡陸象先為僚婿。

translations.literal: At first he married the daughter of He Hui of Kuaiji and was a colleague son-in-law with Lu Xiangxian of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At first he married He Hui's daughter of Kuaiji and was, with Lu Xiangxian of Wu, a colleague son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 象先時為洛陽尉，宰相子，門望甚高。

translations.literal: Xiangxian was then Vice Magistrate of Luoyang, a chief minister's son, of very high lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangxian was then Vice Magistrate of Luoyang, a chief minister's son, of very exalted lineage.

sentences.zh: 嵩尚未入仕，宣州人夏榮稱有相術，謂象先曰：「陸郎十年內位極人臣，然不及蕭郎一門盡貴，官位高而有壽。」

translations.literal: Song had not yet entered office; the Xuancheng man Xia Rong, said to have physiognomic skill, told Xiangxian: "Master Lu within ten years will reach the utmost of human rank, yet he will not equal Master Xiao's whole clan in nobility, high office, and long life.
translations.idiomatic: Song had not yet entered office; Xia Rong of Xuancheng, famed for physiognomy, told Xiangxian, "Within ten years you will reach the summit of rank, yet you will not equal the Xiao clan in nobility, high office, and long life.

sentences.zh: 時人未之許。

translations.literal: People of the time did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time did not believe it.

sentences.zh: 十五年，涼州刺史、河西節度王君滷恃眾每歲攻擊吐蕃。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Military Commissioner of Hexi and Governor of Liangzhou Wang Junhu, relying on his forces, attacked Tibet each year.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Wang Junhu, Military Commissioner of Hexi and Governor of Liangzhou, relying on his troops, attacked Tibet each year.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃大將悉諾邏恭祿及燭龍莽布支攻陷瓜州城，執刺史田元獻及君滷父壽，盡取城中軍資及倉糧，仍毀其城而去。

translations.literal: The Tibetan generals Xinuoluo Gonglu and Zhulong Mangbuzhi captured Guazhou city, seized Governor Tian Yuanxian and Junhu's father Shou, took all military stores and granary grain in the city, and still destroyed the city and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan generals Xinuoluo Gonglu and Zhulong Mangbuzhi took Guazhou, seized Governor Tian Yuanxian and Junhu's father Shou, stripped the city of stores and grain, and destroyed the walls before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 又攻玉門軍及常樂縣，縣令賈師順嬰城固守，賊遂引退。

translations.literal: They also attacked Yumen Army and Changle County; Magistrate Jia Shishun held the city firmly and the bandits then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They also attacked Yumen Army and Changle County; Magistrate Jia Shishun held firm and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 無何，君滷又為回紇諸部殺之於鞏筆驛，河、隴震駭。

translations.literal: Before long Junhu was again killed by the tribes of the Uyghurs at Gongbi Post; He and Long were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Junhu was killed by Uyghur tribes at Gongbi Post; the He and Long region was shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以君滷勇將無謀，果及於難，擇堪邊任者，乃以嵩為兵部尚書、河西節度使，判涼州事。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong, considering Junhu a brave general without stratagem who had indeed met disaster, chose one fit for border duty and therefore made Song Minister of War, Military Commissioner of Hexi, with authority over Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor judged Junhu a brave but unstrategic general who had met disaster; choosing one fit for the border, he made Song Minister of War and Military Commissioner of Hexi with authority over Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 嵩乃請以裴寬、郭虛己、牛仙客在其幕下，又請以建康軍使、左金吾將軍張守珪為瓜州刺史，修築州城，招輯百姓，令其復業。

translations.literal: Song then requested Pei Kuan, Guo Xuji, and Niu Xianke for his staff, and also requested Zhang Shougui, commissioner of Jiankang Army and General of the Left Golden Guards, as Governor of Guazhou to repair the prefectural walls, gather the people, and have them resume their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Song requested Pei Kuan, Guo Xuji, and Niu Xianke for his staff, and Zhang Shougui as Governor of Guazhou to rebuild the walls, gather the people, and restore their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 又加嵩銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Song was further made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Song was further promoted to Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 時悉諾邏恭祿威名甚振，嵩乃縱反間於吐蕃，言其與中國潛通，贊普遂召而誅之。

translations.literal: At the time Xinuoluo Gonglu's reputation was very great; Song therefore spread disinformation in Tibet saying he had secret dealings with China, and the tsenpo summoned and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xinuoluo Gonglu's fame was then very great; Song spread word in Tibet that he dealt secretly with China, and the tsenpo summoned and executed him.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，吐蕃大下，悉末明復率眾攻瓜州，守珪出兵擊走之。

translations.literal: The next autumn Tibet came down in force; Suming again led troops to attack Guazhou, and Shougui led troops out and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: The next autumn Tibet invaded in force; Suming again attacked Guazhou, and Shougui led troops out and repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 隴右節度使、鄯州都督張誌亮引兵至青海西南馮波谷，與吐蕃接戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Longyou and Metropolitan Commissioner of Binzhou Zhang Zhiliang led troops to Fengbo Valley southwest of Qinghai and fought Tibet, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhiliang, Military Commissioner of Longyou, led troops to Fengbo Valley southwest of Qinghai, fought Tibet, and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 八月，嵩又遣副將杜賓客率弩手四千人，與吐蕃戰於祁連城下，自晨至暮，散而復合，賊徒大潰，臨陣斬其副將一人，散走山谷，哭聲四合。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Song again sent Vice General Du Binke with four thousand crossbowmen to fight Tibet below Qilian City; from morning to evening they broke and re-formed; the bandits were greatly routed; one deputy general was beheaded on the field; they scattered into valleys and mountains, wailing on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Song sent Vice General Du Binke with four thousand crossbowmen to fight below Qilian City; from dawn to dusk the enemy broke and re-formed, then collapsed; a deputy was beheaded in battle and the rest fled into the hills, wailing everywhere.

sentences.zh: 露布至，玄宗大悅，乃加嵩同中書門下三品，恩顧莫比。

translations.literal: When the victory report arrived, Emperor Xuanzong was greatly pleased and made Song Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery; his favor was unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: When the victory report arrived, the Emperor was greatly pleased and made Song Associate Chief Minister; none enjoyed such favor.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授宇文融、裴光庭宰相，又加嵩兼中書令。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Yuwen Rong and Pei Guangting were made chief ministers, and Song was further made Chief Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Yuwen Rong and Pei Guangting became chief ministers, and Song was further made Chief Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自十四年燕國公張說罷中書令後，缺此位四年，而嵩居之。

translations.literal: Since Yan State Duke Zhang Yue ceased as Chief Minister of the Secretariat in the fourteenth year, this post had been vacant four years, and Song held it.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhang Yue left the chief ministership in the fourteenth year, the post had been vacant four years until Song filled it.

sentences.zh: 常帶河西節度，遙領之。

translations.literal: He regularly held the Hexi commission and governed it from afar.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to hold the Hexi commission and governed it at a distance.

sentences.zh: 加集賢殿學士、知院事，兼修國史，進位金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was made Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, with charge of the academy and concurrent editing of the national history, and advanced to Golden-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, charged with the academy and editing the national history, and advanced to Golden-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 子衡，尚新昌公主，嵩夫人賀氏入覲拜席，玄宗呼為親家母，禮儀甚盛。

translations.literal: His son Heng married Princess Xinchang; when Song's wife Lady He entered to pay respects, Emperor Xuanzong called her mother-in-law by marriage; the ritual was very grand.
translations.idiomatic: His son Heng married Princess Xinchang; when Lady He paid court respects, the Emperor addressed her as mother-in-law by marriage with great ceremony.

sentences.zh: 尋又進封徐國公。

translations.literal: Soon he was further enfeoffed Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was further enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 二十一年二月，侍中裴光庭卒。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-first year Attendant-in-Chief Pei Guangting died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-first year Attendant-in-Chief Pei Guangting died.

sentences.zh: 光庭與嵩同位數年，情頗不協，及是，玄宗遣嵩擇相，嵩以右丞韓休長者，舉之。

translations.literal: Guangting and Song had been equals for years and their feelings were rather incompatible; at this the Emperor sent Song to choose a chief minister, and Song recommended the Right Vice Director Han Xiu as a man of mature years.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting and Song had long been at odds; the Emperor sent Song to choose a successor, and Song recommended Han Xiu, Right Vice Director, as a man of mature years.

sentences.zh: 及休入相，嵩舉事，休峭直，輒不相假，互於玄宗前論曲直，因讓位。

translations.literal: When Xiu entered the chancellorship, whenever Song proposed affairs Xiu was stern and straight and would not yield; they disputed right and wrong before the Emperor, and Song therefore yielded his post.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu became chief minister, he was stern on every matter Song raised and would not yield; they argued before the throne, and Song yielded his post.

sentences.zh: 玄宗眷嵩厚，乃許嵩授尚書右丞相，令罷相，以休為工部尚書。

translations.literal: The Emperor's regard for Song was thick; he therefore allowed Song to be appointed Right Chief Minister of the Secretariat, to cease as chief minister, with Xiu made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor still favored Song; he allowed him to become Right Chief Minister and leave the chancellorship, making Xiu Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 尋又以嵩子華為給事中。

translations.literal: Soon Song's son Hua was made Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Song's son Hua was made Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，拜太子太師。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 及幽州節度使張守珪坐賂遺中官牛仙童，貶為括州刺史，嵩嘗賄仙童，李林甫發之，貶青州刺史。

translations.literal: When Military Commissioner of Youzhou Zhang Shougui, for bribing the eunuch Niu Xiantong, was demoted to Governor of Kuozhou, Song had once bribed Xiantong; Li Linfu exposed it, and he was demoted to Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shougui was demoted for bribing the eunuch Niu Xiantong, Song's own bribe was exposed by Li Linfu and he was demoted to Governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋又追拜太子太師，嵩又請老。

translations.literal: Soon he was again posthumously recalled as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; Song again requested retirement on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; Song again asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 嵩性好服餌，及罷相，於林園植藥，合煉自適。

translations.literal: Song by nature loved to take medicines and elixirs; after leaving the chancellorship he planted drugs in his grove and garden and compounded them for his own ease.
translations.idiomatic: Song loved medicines and elixirs; after leaving office he planted herbs in his gardens and compounded them for himself.

sentences.zh: 華時為工部侍郎，衡以主婿三品，嵩皤然就養十餘年，家財豐贍，衣冠榮之。

translations.literal: Hua was then Vice Minister of Works and Heng, as imperial son-in-law, third rank; Song, white-haired, received support for more than ten years; family wealth was abundant and robes and caps were glorious.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was Vice Minister of Works and Heng, as imperial son-in-law, held third rank; white-haired, Song was supported more than ten years in wealth and honor.

sentences.zh: 天寶八年薨，年八十餘，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao he died, aged over eighty; he was posthumously made Grand Master of Glorious Affairs with the Same Honors as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianbao he died at over eighty; he was posthumously made Grand Master of Glorious Affairs with the Same Honors as the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 時中官李輔國專典禁兵，怙寵用事，求為宰相，諷宰臣裴冕等薦己，華頗拒之，輔國怒。

translations.literal: At the time the eunuch Li Fuguo exclusively controlled the forbidden troops, relied on favor and acted arbitrarily, sought to be chief minister, and hinted that chief ministers Pei Mian and others recommend him; Hua rather refused, and Fuguo was angry.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Li Fuguo controlled the forbidden troops, sought the chancellorship, and urged Pei Mian and others to recommend him; Hua refused, and Fuguo was enraged.

sentences.zh: 肅宗方寢疾，輔國矯命罷華相位，守禮部尚書，仍引元載代華。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong was then ill in bed; Fuguo forged an order to remove Hua from the chancellorship, keep him as Minister of Rites, and bring in Yuan Zai in Hua's place.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong lay ill; Fuguo forged an order removing Hua from the chancellorship, retaining him as Minister of Rites, and installing Yuan Zai in his place.

sentences.zh: 肅宗崩，代宗在諒暗，元載希輔國旨，貶華為硤州員外司馬，卒於貶所。

translations.literal: When Suzong died, Emperor Daizong was in mourning; Yuan Zai, hoping to please Fuguo, demoted Hua to Vice Administrator of Xia Prefecture and he died in exile.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong died, Daizong was in mourning; Yuan Zai, courting Fuguo, demoted Hua to Vice Administrator of Xia Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 蕭衡、蕭華後人

translations.literal: Descendants of Xiao Heng and Xiao Hua
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of Xiao Heng and Xiao Hua

sentences.zh: 衡子復，德宗朝位亦至宰輔。

translations.literal: Heng's son Fu, in the Dezong reign, also reached the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, son of Heng, also reached the chancellorship under Dezong.

sentences.zh: 華子恆、悟。

translations.literal: Hua's sons Heng and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Hua's sons were Heng and Wu.

sentences.zh: 恆子俯，大和中宰輔。

translations.literal: Heng's son Fu, in the Dahe reign, became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, son of Heng, became chief minister in the Dahe reign.

sentences.zh: 悟子仿，咸通中宰輔，皆自有傳。

translations.literal: Wu's son Fang, chief minister in the Xiantong reign—all have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Fang, son of Wu, was chief minister in Xiantong; each has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 張九齡

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling

sentences.zh: 張九齡，字子壽，一名博物。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling, courtesy name Zishou, had the alternate name Bowen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling, style name Zishou, also called Bowen.

sentences.zh: 曾祖君政，韶州別駕，因家於始興，今為曲江人。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Junzheng was Vice Prefect of Shaozhou and settled the family at Shixing; they are now people of Qujiang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Junzheng was Vice Prefect of Shaozhou and settled the family at Shixing; they are now of Qujiang.

sentences.zh: 父弘愈，以九齡貴，贈廣州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Hongyu, because of Jiuling's eminence, was posthumously made Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hongyu, because of Jiuling's eminence, was posthumously made Governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 九齡幼聰敏，善屬文。

translations.literal: Jiuling was clever and keen from youth and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jiuling was clever and skilled at writing.

sentences.zh: 年十三，以書幹廣州刺史王方慶，大嗟賞之，曰：「此子必能致遠。」

translations.literal: At thirteen he presented writings to Governor Wang Fangqing of Guangzhou, who greatly admired him and said: "This boy is sure to go far.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he presented writings to Governor Wang Fangqing of Guangzhou, who greatly admired him and said, "This boy will surely go far.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，應舉登乙第，拜校書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, answered the examination in the second class, and was appointed Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi, placed in the second class, and was appointed Proofreader.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在東宮，舉天下文藻之士，親加策問，九齡對策高第，遷右拾遺。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong was Heir Apparent he raised men of literary talent throughout the realm and personally examined them by question; Jiuling answered with high rank and was transferred Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor was Heir Apparent he examined literary men throughout the realm; Jiuling ranked high and was made Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 時帝未行親郊之禮，九齡上疏曰：

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor had not yet performed the suburban sacrifice in person; Jiuling memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had not yet performed the suburban sacrifice in person; Jiuling memorialized as follows:

sentences.zh: 伏以天才者，百神之君，而王者之所由受命也。

translations.literal: I consider that Heaven is the lord of the hundred spirits and the source from which kings receive their mandate.
translations.idiomatic: I consider that Heaven is lord of the hundred spirits and the source from which kings receive the mandate.

sentences.zh: 自古繼統之主，必有郊配之義，蓋以敬天命以報所受。

translations.literal: Rulers who succeed to the succession in antiquity all had the meaning of suburban matching sacrifice, thereby revering Heaven's mandate and repaying what they received.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, successive rulers have performed suburban sacrifice to revere Heaven's mandate and repay what they received.

sentences.zh: 故於郊之義，則不以德澤未洽，年谷不登，凡事之故，而闕其禮。

translations.literal: Therefore in the meaning of the suburban sacrifice they did not, because virtue and favor were not yet widespread, harvests were not abundant, or any matter whatsoever, omit this ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore they did not omit the suburban rite for lack of widespread virtue, poor harvests, or any other cause.

sentences.zh: 《孝經》云：「昔者周公郊祀後稷以配天。」

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "In antiquity the Duke of Zhou at the suburban sacrifice matched Hou Ji to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety says, "In antiquity the Duke of Zhou at the suburban sacrifice matched Hou Ji to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 斯謂成王幼沖，周公居攝，猶用其禮，明不暫廢。

translations.literal: This means that when King Cheng was young and the Duke of Zhou held the regency, he still used this ritual, showing it was not briefly suspended.
translations.idiomatic: This means that when King Cheng was young and the Duke held the regency, he still performed the rite—it was not set aside.

sentences.zh: 漢丞相匡衡亦云：「帝王之事，莫重乎郊祀。」

translations.literal: Han Chancellor Kuang Heng also said: "Among the affairs of emperors and kings, nothing is heavier than the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Kuang Heng of Han also said, "Among royal affairs nothing outweighs the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 董仲舒又云：「不郊而祭山川，失祭之序，逆於禮正，故《春秋》非之。」

translations.literal: Dong Zhongshu again said: "Without the suburban sacrifice yet sacrificing to mountains and rivers loses the order of sacrifice and violates ritual propriety; therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals condemns it."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu said, "To sacrifice to mountains and rivers without the suburban rite reverses proper order; the Spring and Autumn Annals condemns it."

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為匡衡、仲舒，古之知禮者，皆謂郊之為祭所宜先也。

translations.literal: I consider that Kuang Heng and Dong Zhongshu, knowers of ritual in antiquity, all said the suburban sacrifice should come first among sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang Heng and Dong Zhongshu, ancient masters of ritual, held that the suburban rite must precede all others.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下紹休聖緒，其命惟新，御極已來，於今五載，既光太平之業，未行大報之禮，竊考經傳，義或未通。

translations.literal: I consider that Your Majesty continues the sage succession; the mandate is anew; since taking the throne, it is now five years—you have already illumined the enterprise of great peace yet have not performed the great reporting sacrifice; examining the classics and commentaries, the meaning may not be fully clear.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty continues the sage succession; five years have passed since you took the throne—you have achieved great peace yet not the great reporting sacrifice; by the classics, this may be amiss.

sentences.zh: 今百穀嘉生，鳥獸咸若，夷狄內附，兵革用寧。

translations.literal: Now the hundred grains flourish, birds and beasts all comply, barbarians submit within, and weapons and armor are at rest.
translations.idiomatic: Now grain flourishes, beasts thrive, barbarians submit, and arms rest.

sentences.zh: 將欲鑄劍為農，泥金封禪，用彰功德之美，允答神只之心。

translations.literal: You wish to cast swords into ploughshares, seal merit with gold dust, manifest the beauty of merit and virtue, and answer the hearts of spirits and gods.
translations.idiomatic: You would cast swords into ploughshares and seal merit on Mount Tai, manifesting virtue and answering the spirits.

sentences.zh: 能事畢行，光耀帝載。

translations.literal: When the affair is completed and carried out, it will illumine the Emperor's record.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite is fully performed, it will glorify the imperial record.

sentences.zh: 況郊祀常典，猶闕其儀，有若怠於事天，臣恐不可以訓。

translations.literal: Moreover the suburban sacrifice is a constant canon, yet its ritual is still lacking; it is as if one were slack in serving Heaven—I fear this cannot serve as instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The suburban sacrifice is a standing rite, yet its observance is still lacking—as if Heaven were neglected, which I fear cannot instruct the realm.

sentences.zh: 伏望以迎日之至，展焚柴之禮，升紫壇，陳采席，定天位，明天道，則聖朝典則，可謂無遺矣。

translations.literal: I beg that at the arrival of the day to welcome the sun you unfold the ritual of burning firewood, ascend the purple altar, spread the colored mat, fix Heaven's position, and clarify Heaven's Way—then the sacred dynasty's canon may be said to leave nothing out.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that at the winter solstice you perform the firewood-burning rite, ascend the purple altar, spread the colored mat, fix Heaven's position and clarify Heaven's Way—then the court's ritual canon will be complete.

sentences.zh: 九齡以才鑒見推，當時吏部試拔萃選人及應舉者，咸令九齡與右拾遺趙冬曦考其等第，前後數四，每稱平允。

translations.literal: Jiuling was recommended for his talent and discernment; at the time when the Ministry of Personnel tested outstanding candidates for selection and those answering the examinations, all were ordered examined for grade by Jiuling and Right Reminder Zhao Dongxi, four or five times in succession, and each time they were called fair and even.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling was esteemed for talent and judgment; whenever the Ministry tested candidates, Jiuling and Right Reminder Zhao Dongxi graded them several times, and each round was praised as fair.

sentences.zh: 開元十年，三遷司勛員外郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan he was thrice promoted to Vice Director of the Merit Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan he was promoted three times to Vice Director of the Merit Section.

sentences.zh: 時張說為中書令，與九齡同姓，敘為昭穆，尤親重之，常謂人曰：「後來詞人稱首也。」

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Yue was Chief Minister of the Secretariat; he shared a surname with Jiuling and treated him as a collateral clansman, especially valuing him, and often told people: "Among later men of letters he will be first.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue was then Chief Minister; sharing Jiuling's surname, he treated him as kin and often said, "Among later writers he will stand first.

sentences.zh: 九齡既欣知己，亦依附焉。

translations.literal: Jiuling, delighted at finding a confidant, also attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted at such patronage, Jiuling attached himself to Yue as well.

sentences.zh: 十一年，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was appointed Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十三年，車駕東巡，行封禪之禮。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the imperial carriage toured east and performed the feng and shan sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Emperor traveled east and performed the feng and shan rites.

sentences.zh: 說自定侍從升中之官，多引兩省錄事主書及己之所親攝官而上，遂加特進階，超授五品。

translations.literal: Yue himself fixed the officials who would accompany the ascent to the central peak; he largely brought up registrars and chief clerks of the two Secretariats and his own intimates in acting posts, and therefore specially advanced them in rank, promoting them beyond the fifth grade.
translations.idiomatic: Yue chose who would attend the central ascent, elevating many registrars, clerks, and his own intimates to acting posts and promoting them past the fifth grade.

sentences.zh: 初，令九齡草詔，九齡言於說曰：「官爵者，天下之公器，德望為先，勞舊次焉。

translations.literal: At first he ordered Jiuling to draft the edict; Jiuling spoke to Yue: "Office and rank are the public vessels of the realm; virtue and reputation come first, merit and seniority next.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling was told to draft the edict and told Yue, "Rank is the realm's public vessel—virtue and reputation first, merit and seniority next.

sentences.zh: 若顛倒衣裳，則譏謗起矣。

translations.literal: If you turn garments upside down, ridicule and slander will arise.
translations.idiomatic: If you invert rank and merit, scandal will follow.

sentences.zh: 今登封霈澤，千載一遇。

translations.literal: Now the grace of the feng sacrifice is a meeting once in a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: The feng grace comes once in a millennium.

sentences.zh: 清流高品，不沐殊恩。

translations.literal: The clear current and high grades do not bathe in special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Men of clear reputation and high rank receive no special favor.

sentences.zh: 胥吏末班，先加章紱。

translations.literal: Petty clerks in the lowest ranks are first given seals and ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: Low clerks are first given seals and ribbons.

sentences.zh: 但恐制出之後，四方失望。

translations.literal: I fear only that after the edict issues, the four quarters will be disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that when the edict appears, the realm will be disappointed.

sentences.zh: 今進草之際，事猶可改，唯令公審籌之，無貽後悔也。」

translations.literal: While the draft is still advancing, the matter can still be changed; I beg the Chief Minister to consider carefully and leave no regret.
translations.idiomatic: The draft can still be changed; I beg you consider carefully and leave no regret.

sentences.zh: 說曰：「事已決矣，悠悠之談，何足慮也！」

translations.literal: Yue said: "The matter is already decided; idle talk—why worry!"
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "It is decided—idle gossip is not worth heeding!"

sentences.zh: 竟不從。

translations.literal: In the end he did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: He would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及制出，內外甚咎於說。

translations.literal: When the edict issued, inside and outside greatly blamed Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict appeared, court and country blamed Yue.

sentences.zh: 時御史中丞宇文融方知田戶之事，每有所奏，說多建議違之，融亦以此不平於說。

translations.literal: At the time Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong had just mastered the matter of field households; whenever he memorialized, Yue often proposed contrary views, and Rong therefore was also discontent with Yue on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Rong had mastered field-household policy; Yue often opposed his memorials, and Rong resented him.

sentences.zh: 九齡復勸說為備，說又不從其言。

translations.literal: Jiuling again urged Yue to take precautions; Yue again did not follow his words.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling again urged precaution; Yue again refused.

sentences.zh: 無幾，說果為融所劾，罷知政事，九齡亦改太常少卿，尋出為冀暫刺史。

translations.literal: Before long Yue was indeed impeached by Rong, ceased handling government affairs, and Jiuling was also changed to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and soon sent out as Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yue was impeached by Rong and left office; Jiuling became Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was sent to Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 九齡以母老在鄉，而河北道里遼遠，上疏固請換江南一州，望得數承母音耗，優制許之，改為洪州都督。

translations.literal: Jiuling, because his mother was old in his home district and the Hebei route was very far, firmly memorialized asking to exchange for a Jiangnan prefecture, hoping to receive his mother's news several times; a gracious edict granted it and he was changed to Military Commissioner of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was old at home and Hebei was remote; he begged a Jiangnan post to hear from her, and was made Military Commissioner of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄轉桂州都督，仍充嶺南道按察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred Military Commissioner of Guizhou and still served as Investigating Commissioner of the Lingnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Guizhou and still served as Investigating Commissioner of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 上又以其弟九章、九臯為嶺南道刺史，令歲時伏臘，皆得寧覲。

translations.literal: The Emperor also made his younger brothers Jiuzhang and Jiugao Governors of Lingnan so that at the seasonal festivals they could all visit their parents in peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also appointed his brothers Jiuzhang and Jiugao to Lingnan so they could visit their parents at the festivals.

sentences.zh: 初，張說知集賢院事，常薦九齡堪為學士，以備顧問。

translations.literal: At first Zhang Yue, knowing affairs of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, often recommended Jiuling as fit to be an academician to supply consultation.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue directed the Hall of Assembled Worthies he often recommended Jiuling as an academician for counsel.

sentences.zh: 說卒後，上思其言，召拜九齡為秘書少監、集賢院學士，副知院事。

translations.literal: After Yue died the Emperor recalled his words and summoned Jiuling as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Academician of the Hall, with deputy charge of the academy.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue's death the Emperor recalled his words and made Jiuling Vice Director of the Secretariat and Academician with deputy charge of the hall.

sentences.zh: 再遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was again promoted Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted Vice Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 常密有陳奏，多見納用。

translations.literal: He often secretly memorialized and much was adopted and used.
translations.idiomatic: He often memorialized in secret and much was adopted.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母喪歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Soon he mourned his mother and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he mourned his mother and returned home.

sentences.zh: 二十一年十二月，起復拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the twenty-first year he was recalled from mourning and appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister.
