translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the twenty-first year he was recalled from mourning as Vice Minister and Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷中書令，兼修國史。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred Chief Minister of the Secretariat and concurrently edited the national history.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became Chief Minister of the Secretariat and edited the national history.

sentences.zh: 時范陽節度使張守珪以裨將安祿山討奚、契丹敗衄，執送京師，請行朝典。

translations.literal: At the time Military Commissioner of Fanyang Zhang Shougui, because his subordinate general An Lushan in campaigning against the Xi and Khitan suffered defeat, sent him bound to the capital and requested court punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shougui sent his subordinate An Lushan to the capital in bonds after a defeat against the Xi and Khitan and asked for punishment.

sentences.zh: 九齡奏劾曰：「穰苴出軍，必誅莊賈；

translations.literal: Jiuling memorialized impeaching: "When Rang Ju led the army he had to execute Zhuang Jia;
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling memorialized, "When Rang Ju took the field he executed Zhuang Jia;

sentences.zh: 孫武教戰，亦斬宮嬪。

translations.literal: when Sun Wu taught battle he also beheaded palace women.
translations.idiomatic: when Sun Wu trained troops he beheaded palace women.

sentences.zh: 守珪軍令必行，祿山不宜免死。」

translations.literal: Shougui's military orders must be carried out; Lushan should not escape death.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui's orders must stand; Lushan ought not be spared.

sentences.zh: 上特舍之。

translations.literal: The Emperor specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor specially pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 九齡奏曰：「祿山狼子野心，面有逆相，臣請因罪戮之，冀絕後患。」

translations.literal: Jiuling memorialized: "Lushan has the heart of a wolf cub and a rebellious countenance on his face; I beg to execute him for his crime and cut off later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling said, "Lushan has a wolf's heart and a traitor's face; execute him now and forestall later harm.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿勿以王夷甫知石勒故事，誤害忠良。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Do not, like Wang Yifu knowing the story of Shi Le, wrongly harm a loyal man."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Do not, like Wang Yifu with Shi Le, wrongly kill a loyal man."

sentences.zh: 遂放歸籓。

translations.literal: He was therefore released back to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He was released back to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加金紫光祿大夫，累封始興縣伯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was made Golden-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed in succession as Baron of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was made Golden-Gleam Grand Master and enfeoffed Baron of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 李林甫自無學術，以九齡文行為上所知，心頗忌之。

translations.literal: Li Linfu himself had no learning; because Jiuling's literary conduct was known to the Emperor, he was quite jealous in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu lacked learning; jealous that the Emperor knew Jiuling's literary merit, he resented him.

sentences.zh: 乃引牛仙客知政事，九齡屢言不可，帝不悅。

translations.literal: He therefore brought in Niu Xianke to handle government affairs; Jiuling repeatedly said it could not be, and the Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He brought in Niu Xianke; Jiuling repeatedly objected, and the Emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，遷尚書右丞相，罷知政事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred Right Chief Minister of the Secretariat and ceased handling government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he became Right Chief Minister and left the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 後宰執每薦引公卿，上必問：「風度得如九齡否？」

translations.literal: Later whenever chief ministers recommended dukes and ministers, the Emperor always asked: "Is his bearing like Jiuling's?
translations.idiomatic: Whenever ministers were recommended, the Emperor asked, "Is his bearing like Jiuling's?

sentences.zh: 故事皆搢笏於帶，而後乘馬，九齡體羸，常使人持之，因設笏囊。

translations.literal: By precedent all tucked the memorial tablet in the belt and then mounted horse; Jiuling's body was frail and he regularly had someone hold it, and therefore a tablet pouch was devised.
translations.idiomatic: By custom officials tucked the tablet in the belt before riding; frail, Jiuling had it carried for him, and the tablet pouch was invented.

sentences.zh: 笏囊之設，自九齡始也。

translations.literal: The setting of the tablet pouch began with Jiuling.
translations.idiomatic: The tablet pouch began with Jiuling.

sentences.zh: 初，九齡為相，薦長安尉周子諒為監察御史。

translations.literal: When Jiuling first became chief minister he recommended Chang'an Vice Magistrate Zhou Ziliang as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister he recommended Zhou Ziliang, Vice Magistrate of Chang'an, as Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 至是，子諒以妄陳休咎，上親加詰問，令於朝堂決殺之。

translations.literal: By this time Ziliang, for rashly stating omens, was personally interrogated by the Emperor and ordered executed by collective decision in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang rashly spoke of omens; the Emperor interrogated him and ordered him executed in court.

sentences.zh: 九齡坐引非其人，左遷荊州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Jiuling, for having introduced an unfit man, was demoted Chief Administrator of the Metropolitan Area of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For recommending the wrong man, Jiuling was demoted Chief Administrator of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄請歸拜墓，因遇疾卒，年六十八，贈荊州大都督，謚曰文獻。

translations.literal: Soon he requested leave to return and visit his parents' tombs; he encountered illness and died, aged sixty-eight; he was posthumously made Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhou, posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked to visit the family tombs, fell ill and died at sixty-eight; he was posthumously Governor of Jingzhou, title Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 九齡在相位時，建議復置十道采訪使，又教河南數州水種稻，以廣屯田。

translations.literal: When Jiuling was in the chief minister's post he proposed restoring the ten investigating commissioners and taught several prefectures south of the Yellow River to plant rice in wet fields to expand garrison fields.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister he proposed restoring ten investigating commissioners and teaching Henan prefectures to plant rice for garrison fields.

sentences.zh: 議置屯田，費功無利，竟不能就，罷之。

translations.literal: The proposal to establish garrison fields cost labor without profit and in the end could not be completed; it was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison-field plan cost labor without profit and was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 性頗躁急，動輒忿詈，議者以此少之。

translations.literal: His nature was rather impatient; he often burst into angry reviling on impulse, and critics therefore thought somewhat less of him.
translations.idiomatic: He was quick-tempered and prone to angry outbursts, for which critics faulted him.

sentences.zh: 子拯，伊闕令。

translations.literal: His son Zheng was Magistrate of Yique.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng was Magistrate of Yique.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂陷賊，不受偽命。

translations.literal: In the An Lushan rebellion he fell into the bandits' hands but did not accept false orders.
translations.idiomatic: In the rebellion he was captured but refused rebel orders.

sentences.zh: 兩京克復，詔加太子右贊善。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were recovered, an edict added him Right Supporter of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the capitals were recovered, he was made Right Supporter of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 弟九臯，自尚書郎歷唐、徐、宋、襄、廣五州刺史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jiugao, from Director in the Ministry, served in succession as Governor of Tang, Xu, Song, Xiang, and Guang.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Jiugao rose from Ministry Director to five governorships.

sentences.zh: 九章，歷吉、明、曹三州刺史，鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: Jiuzhang served in succession as Governor of Ji, Ming, and Cao and as Director of the Court for Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuzhang governed Ji, Ming, and Cao and became Director of the Court for Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 九齡為中書令時，天長節百僚上壽，多獻珍異，唯九齡進《金鏡錄》五卷，言前古興廢之道，上賞異之。

translations.literal: When Jiuling was Chief Minister of the Secretariat, on the Emperor's birthday the hundred officials offered longevity congratulations and mostly presented rare treasures; only Jiuling presented five scrolls of the Record of the Golden Mirror, speaking of the rise and fall of former ages, and the Emperor greatly prized it.
translations.idiomatic: On the Emperor's birthday, while others gave treasures, Jiuling presented five scrolls of the Record of the Golden Mirror on the rise and fall of dynasties, which the Emperor greatly prized.

sentences.zh: 又與中書侍郎嚴挺之、尚書左丞袁仁敬、右庶子梁升卿、御史中丞盧怡結交友善。

translations.literal: He also with Vice Minister of the Secretariat Yan Tingzhi, Left Assistant Chief Minister Yuan Renjing, Right Companion Liang Shengqing, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Lu Yi formed a bond of friendship.
translations.idiomatic: He befriended Yan Tingzhi, Yuan Renjing, Liang Shengqing, and Lu Yi.

sentences.zh: 挺之等有才幹，而交道終始不渝，甚為當時之所稱。

translations.literal: Tingzhi and the others had talent and ability, and their friendship from beginning to end never changed, greatly praised by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: They were talented men whose friendship never wavered, much praised at the time.

sentences.zh: 至德初，上皇在蜀，思九齡之先覺，下詔褒贈，曰：「正大廈者柱石之力，昌帝業者輔相之臣。

translations.literal: In early Zhide the Retired Emperor was in Shu, recalling Jiuling's foresight, and issued an edict of praise and posthumous gift, saying: "To raise a great hall takes the strength of pillars and beams; to flourish an imperial enterprise takes assisting ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide the Retired Emperor in Shu recalled Jiuling's foresight and praised him: "Great halls need pillars; great enterprises need ministers.

sentences.zh: 生則保其榮名，歿乃稱其盛德，節終未允於人望，加贈實存乎國章。

translations.literal: In life preserve their honored names; in death praise their great virtue—when the end does not satisfy human expectation, added posthumous gifts truly remain in the state's regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Honor them in life and praise them in death—when the end falls short, added gifts remain in the state's law.

sentences.zh: 故中書令張九齡，維嶽降神，濟川作相，開元之際，寅亮成功。

translations.literal: The former Chief Minister of the Secretariat Zhang Jiuling—spirit descended from the great peak, a raft-pole minister across the ford; in the Kaiyuan era he assisted in brightness and success.
translations.idiomatic: Former Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling—spirit of the peak, minister across the ford; in Kaiyuan he lit the age.

sentences.zh: 讜言定其社稷，先覺合於蓍策，永懷賢弼，可謂大臣。

translations.literal: Straight words settled the altars of soil and grain; foresight matched the yarrow stalks; ever cherishing such a worthy assistant, one may call him a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: His counsel secured the realm; his foresight matched the oracle; he was truly a great minister.

sentences.zh: 竹帛猶存，樵蘇必禁，爰從八命之秩，更進三臺之位。

translations.literal: Silk and bamboo still remain; fuel and kindling must be forbidden; love moves from the rank of eight orders to advance to the position of the Three Terraces.
translations.idiomatic: His records remain; his tomb must be protected; let his rank rise to the Three Terraces.

sentences.zh: 可贈司徒，仍遣使就韶州致祭。」

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made Minister of Education; still send an envoy to Shaozhou to perform sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously make him Minister of Education and send sacrifice to Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 張仲方

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongfang
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongfang

sentences.zh: 九臯曾孫仲方，少朗秀。

translations.literal: Jiugao's great-grandson Zhongfang was bright and elegant from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Jiugao's great-grandson Zhongfang was bright and refined from boyhood.

sentences.zh: 為兒童時，父友高郢見而奇之，曰；

translations.literal: When he was a child his father's friend Gao Ying saw him and marveled, saying:
translations.idiomatic: As a boy, Gao Ying, his father's friend, marveled and said,

sentences.zh: 「此子非常，必為國器，吾獲高位，必振發之。」

translations.literal: "This boy is extraordinary and is sure to be a pillar of the state; if I obtain high rank I am sure to raise him up.
translations.idiomatic: "This boy is extraordinary and will be a pillar of the state; if I rise high I will raise him up.

sentences.zh: 後郢為御史大夫，首請仲方為御史。

translations.literal: Later when Ying was Censor-in-Chief he first requested Zhongfang as censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying became Censor-in-Chief he first made Zhongfang a censor.

sentences.zh: 歷金州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as Governor of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Governor of Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 郡人有田產為中人所奪，仲方三疏奏聞，竟理其冤。

translations.literal: A man in the prefecture had fields seized by a eunuch; Zhongfang memorialized three times and finally righted the injustice.
translations.idiomatic: When a eunuch seized a man's fields, Zhongfang memorialized thrice and righted the wrong.

sentences.zh: 入為度支郎中，駁李吉甫謚，吉甫之黨惡之，出為遂州司馬。

translations.literal: He entered office as Director in the Revenue Section and rejected Li Jifu's posthumous title; Jifu's faction hated him and he was sent out as Vice Magistrate of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: As Revenue Director he opposed Li Jifu's posthumous title; Jifu's faction sent him to Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 稍遷復、曹、鄭三郡守。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred Administrator of Fu, Cao, and Zheng prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Fu, Cao, and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was made Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: He became Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 時鄠縣令崔發因辱小黃門，敬宗赫怒，付臺推鞫。

translations.literal: At the time Magistrate of E County Cui Fa, for insulting a junior yellow-gate attendant, aroused Jing Zong's rage; he was handed to the censorate for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Cui Fa insulted a junior eunuch; Jing Zong in rage sent him to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 及元日大赦，獨發不得宥。

translations.literal: At the New Year great amnesty, Fa alone was not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: At the New Year amnesty, Fa alone was excluded.

sentences.zh: 仲方上疏，其略曰：「鴻恩將布於天下，而不行御前；

translations.literal: Zhongfang memorialized, in summary: "The great favor is about to be spread under Heaven yet does not reach one before the throne;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang memorialized in summary, "Mercy spreads under Heaven yet not before the throne;

sentences.zh: 霈澤始被於昆蟲，而獨遺崔發。」

translations.literal: the generous dew begins to touch insects yet Fa alone is left out.
translations.idiomatic: grace touches even insects yet Cui Fa is left out.

sentences.zh: 由是發得不死，時論美之。

translations.literal: Because of this Fa did not die, and opinion of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Fa was spared, and contemporaries praised Zhongfang.

sentences.zh: 大和九年，為京兆尹，將相從累者皆大戮，仲方密令識之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dahe he was Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao; when chiefs and ministers who followed were all greatly slaughtered, Zhongfang secretly ordered them identified.
translations.idiomatic: In Dahe 9, as Metropolitan Governor, when slaughtered ministers were piled up, he secretly had them identified.

sentences.zh: 旋詔下許令收葬，得認遺骸，實仲方之力也。

translations.literal: Soon an edict permitted burial; recognizing the remains was truly Zhongfang's doing.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then allowed burial; identifying the dead was his work.

sentences.zh: 是時軍人橫恣，仲方脂韋，坐不稱職，出為華州刺史，改秘書監。

translations.literal: At the time soldiers acted violently; Zhongfang appeased Wei and, for not fulfilling his post, was sent out Governor of Hua Prefecture and changed to Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: When soldiers ran wild, he appeased Wei but was judged unfit and made Governor of Hua, then Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 開成二年卒，年七十二，贈禮部尚書，謚曰成。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng he died, aged seventy-two; he was posthumously made Minister of Rites, posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaicheng 2 he died at seventy-two; posthumously Minister of Rites, title Cheng.

sentences.zh: 李適之

translations.literal: Li Shizhi
translations.idiomatic: Li Shizhi

sentences.zh: 李適之，一名昌，恆山王承乾之孫也。

translations.literal: Li Shizhi, alternate name Chang, was grandson of Prince of Hengshan Chengqian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shizhi, also called Chang, was grandson of Prince Chengqian of Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 父象，官至懷州別駕。

translations.literal: His father Xiang reached Vice Prefect of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiang rose to Vice Prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 適之神龍初起家拜左衛郎將。

translations.literal: Shizhi at the start of Shenlong entered office as Left Guard Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shenlong Shizhi entered office as Left Guard Commandant.

sentences.zh: 開元中，累遷通州刺史，以強幹見稱。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan he rose in succession to Governor of Tong Prefecture and was praised for forceful capability.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan he rose to Governor of Tong and was praised as forceful.

sentences.zh: 時給事中韓朝宗為按察使，特表薦之，擢拜秦州都督。

translations.literal: At the time Drafting Attendant Han Chaozong was Investigating Commissioner and specially memorialized recommending him; he was promoted Military Commissioner of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Han Chaozong, investigating commissioner, recommended him; he became Military Commissioner of Qin.

sentences.zh: 俄轉陜州刺史，入為河南尹。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred Governor of Shan Prefecture and entered office as Metropolitan Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he governed Shan and then became Metropolitan Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 適之性簡率，不務苛細，人吏便之。

translations.literal: Shizhi's nature was plain and direct; he did not pursue harsh detail, and clerks and people found him convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and direct, he avoided petty severity and was convenient to clerks and people.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 開元二十七年，兼幽州大都督府長史，知節度事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Kaiyuan he concurrently served as Chief Administrator of the Metropolitan Area of Youzhou and knew military affairs as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 27 he concurrently commanded Youzhou and knew military affairs.

sentences.zh: 適之以祖得罪見廢，父又遭則天所黜，葬禮有闕，上疏請歸葬昭陵之闕內。

translations.literal: Shizhi, because his grandfather was condemned and deposed and his father again suffered demotion by Empress Wu, with funeral rites deficient, memorialized asking to return and bury within the gap of Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was condemned and his father demoted by Empress Wu; with funeral rites lacking, he begged burial in the gap at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 於是下詔追贈承乾為恆山湣王，象為越州都督、郇國公，伯父厥及亡兄數人並有褒贈。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued posthumously enfeoffing Chengqian as Prince Min of Hengshan, Xiang as Metropolitan Commissioner of Yuezhou and Duke of Xun, and the paternal uncle Jue and several deceased elder brothers all received praise and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made Chengqian Prince Min of Hengshan, Xiang Duke of Xun and Commissioner of Yue, and honored several deceased kin.

sentences.zh: 數喪同至京師，葬禮甚盛，仍刊石於墳所。

translations.literal: Several funerals arrived together in the capital; the burial rites were very grand, and stone was still carved at the grave site.
translations.idiomatic: Several coffins came to the capital together; the burials were splendid, with stone carved at the graves.

sentences.zh: 俄拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 適之雅好賓友，飲酒一斗不亂，夜則宴賞，晝決公務，庭無留事。

translations.literal: Shizhi by nature loved guests and friends; he drank a dou without disorder, feasted and rewarded at night, and decided public affairs by day, with nothing left pending in the court.
translations.idiomatic: He loved guests, could drink a dou without losing composure, feasted at night and cleared the docket by day.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，代牛仙客為左相，累封清和縣公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao he replaced Niu Xianke as Left Chief Minister and was enfeoffed in succession as Duke of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 he replaced Niu Xianke as Left Chief Minister and was enfeoffed Duke of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 與李林甫爭權不葉，適之性疏，為其陰中。

translations.literal: He contended with Li Linfu for power and fell out; Shizhi's nature was loose, and Linfu struck at him in secret.
translations.idiomatic: He vied with Li Linfu for power; loose by nature, Shizhi was undermined in secret.

sentences.zh: 林甫嘗謂適之曰：「華山有金鑛，采之可以富國，上未之知。」

translations.literal: Linfu once told Shizhi: "Mount Hua has gold mines; mining them could enrich the state—the Emperor does not yet know.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu told Shizhi, "Mount Hua has gold mines that could enrich the state—the Emperor does not know.

sentences.zh: 適之心善其言，他日從容奏之。

translations.literal: Shizhi thought well of his words and on another day calmly memorialized them.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi liked the idea and later memorialized it at leisure.

sentences.zh: 玄宗大悅，顧問林甫，對曰：「臣知之久矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was greatly pleased and asked Linfu, who replied: "Your servant has known it long.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was delighted and asked Linfu, who said, "I have known it long.

sentences.zh: 然華山陛下本命，王氣所在，不可穿鑿，臣故不敢上言。」

translations.literal: But Mount Hua is Your Majesty's natal mountain, where royal qi resides—it must not be drilled; your servant therefore dared not speak above.
translations.idiomatic: But Mount Hua is Your Majesty's natal mountain, seat of royal qi—it must not be mined; I dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 帝以為愛己，薄適之言疏。

translations.literal: The Emperor thought him loving toward himself and thought Shizhi's words loose.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thought Linfu cared for him and deemed Shizhi careless.

sentences.zh: 隴右節度皇甫惟明、刑部尚書韋堅、戶部尚書裴寬、京兆尹韓朝宗，悉與適之善，林甫皆中傷之，構成其罪，相繼放逐。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Longyou Huangfu Weiming, Minister of Punishments Wei Jian, Minister of Revenue Pei Kuan, and Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao Han Chaozong were all friendly with Shizhi; Linfu slandered them all, fabricated crimes, and they were exiled in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Weiming, Wei Jian, Pei Kuan, and Han Chaozong were Shizhi's friends; Linfu slandered them into exile one after another.

sentences.zh: 適之懼不自安，求為散職。

translations.literal: Shizhi, in fear, could not be at ease and sought an honorary post.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for himself, Shizhi sought an honorary post.

sentences.zh: 五載，罷知政事，守太子少保。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he ceased handling government affairs and remained Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he left office and kept the post of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 遽命親故歡會，賦詩曰：「避賢初罷相，樂聖且銜杯。

translations.literal: He at once ordered kin and friends to feast together and composed a poem: "Having first left office to yield to the worthy, I now enjoy the sage and hold the cup.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned kin and friends and wrote, "Having left office to yield to the worthy, I enjoy the sage and hold the cup.

sentences.zh: 為問門前客，今朝幾個來？」

translations.literal: I ask the guests before my gate—how many come today?
translations.idiomatic: I ask the guests at my gate—how many come today?

sentences.zh: 竟坐與韋堅等相善，貶宜春太守。

translations.literal: In the end, for being friendly with Wei Jian and others, he was demoted Governor of Yichun.
translations.idiomatic: For friendship with Wei Jian and others he was demoted Governor of Yichun.

sentences.zh: 後御史羅希奭奉使殺韋堅、盧幼臨、裴敦復、李邕等於貶所，州縣且聞希奭到，無不惶駭。

translations.literal: Later Investigating Censor Luo Xiyi was sent to kill Wei Jian, Lu Youlin, Pei Dunfu, Li Yong and others in their places of exile; prefectures and counties, hearing Xiyi was coming, were all terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xiyi was sent to kill exiles including Wei Jian; wherever his mission was heard, terror spread.

sentences.zh: 希奭過宜春郡，適之聞其來，仰藥而死。

translations.literal: When Xiyi passed Yichun Prefecture, Shizhi, hearing he was coming, took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiyi reached Yichun, Shizhi heard of it and took poison.

sentences.zh: 李季卿

translations.literal: Li Jiqing
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiqing

sentences.zh: 子季卿，弱冠舉明經，頗工文詞。

translations.literal: His son Jiqing, at twenty answered the Classics examination and was quite skilled at literary phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiqing, at twenty, passed the Classics exam and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 應制舉，登博學宏詞科，再遷京兆府鄠縣尉。

translations.literal: He answered the imperial examination, passed the Broad Learning and Grand Phrasing category, and was twice promoted Vice Magistrate of E County in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Broad Learning and Grand Phrasing exam and became Vice Magistrate of E in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 肅宗朝，累遷中書舍人，以公事坐貶通州別駕。

translations.literal: In the Suzong reign he rose in succession to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat and, for a public matter, was demoted Vice Prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Suzong he rose to Drafting Attendant, then was demoted Vice Prefect of Tong for a public offense.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，大舉淹抑，自通州徵為京兆少尹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong took the throne he greatly raised the long-suppressed; from Tong Prefecture Jiqing was summoned as Vice Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong succeeded, he recalled the long-suppressed; Jiqing was summoned from Tong as Vice Governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 尋復中書舍人，拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was again Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again Drafting Attendant and Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 俄兼御史大夫，奉使河南、江淮宣慰，振拔幽滯，進用忠廉，時人稱之。

translations.literal: Soon he also served as Vice Censor-in-Chief, was sent to comfort Henan and the Jiang-Huai region, raised the obscure and stagnant, and promoted the loyal and incorrupt—people of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: As Vice Censor-in-Chief he comforted Henan and Jiang-Huai, promoted the neglected and the loyal, and won praise.

sentences.zh: 在銓衡數年，轉右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the balance of appointments for several years he was transferred Right Regular Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in appointments he became Right Regular Cavalier Attendant.

sentences.zh: 季卿有宇量，性識博達，善與人交，襟懷豁如。

translations.literal: Jiqing had breadth of capacity, knowledge broad and penetrating, was good at dealing with people, and his breast was open as if cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqing was broad-minded, learned, sociable, and open-hearted.

sentences.zh: 其在朝以進賢為務，士以此多之。

translations.literal: In court he made advancing the worthy his task, and gentlemen therefore thought much of him.
translations.idiomatic: At court he made promoting talent his task, and gentlemen esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 大曆二年卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dali he died; he was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 2 he died and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 孫融，立性嚴整，善吏事。

translations.literal: His grandson Rong had a stern, orderly nature and was skilled at administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Rong was stern and skilled in administration.

sentences.zh: 貞元十年，歷官至渭州節度使卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenyuan he rose in office to Military Commissioner of Wei Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 10 he reached Military Commissioner of Wei and died.

sentences.zh: 嚴挺之

translations.literal: Yan Tingzhi
translations.idiomatic: Yan Tingzhi

sentences.zh: 嚴挺之，華州華陰人。

translations.literal: Yan Tingzhi was a man of Huayin in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Tingzhi was a native of Huayin in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 叔父方嶷，景雲中戶部郎中。

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Fangdie was Director in the Ministry of Revenue in the Jingyun era.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Fangdie was a Ministry of Revenue director in Jingyun.

sentences.zh: 挺之少好學，舉進士。

translations.literal: Tingzhi from youth loved learning and answered the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Tingzhi loved learning and passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，制舉擢第，授義興尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong he passed the decree examination with high rank and was appointed Vice Magistrate of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong 1 he passed the decree exam and was appointed Vice Magistrate of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 遇姚崇為常州刺史，見其體質昂藏，雅有吏幹，深器異之。

translations.literal: He met Yao Chong as Governor of Changzhou; seeing his imposing physique and elegant administrative ability, Chong greatly prized and marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chong was Governor of Changzhou he saw Tingzhi's imposing bearing and prized his talent.

sentences.zh: 及崇再入為中書令，引挺之為右拾遺。

translations.literal: When Chong again entered office as Chief Minister of the Secretariat he brought in Tingzhi as Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong again became chief minister he made Tingzhi Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 睿宗好樂，聽之忘倦，玄宗又善音律。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong loved music and listened until he forgot weariness; Emperor Xuanzong was also skilled in music and tones.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong loved music to the point of weariness; Xuanzong too was skilled in music.

sentences.zh: 先天二年正月望，胡僧婆陀請夜開門燃百千燈，睿宗禦延喜門觀樂，凡經四日。

translations.literal: On the first-month full moon of the second year of Xiantian, the Hu monk Botuo requested opening the gates at night to light a hundred thousand lamps; Ruizong attended at Yanxi Gate to view the music for four days in all.
translations.idiomatic: On the Xiantian 2 first-month full moon the monk Botuo asked to open the gates at night for lamps; Ruizong watched from Yanxi Gate for four days.

sentences.zh: 又追作先天元年大酺，睿宗禦安福門樓觀百司酺宴，以夜繼晝，經月餘日。

translations.literal: They again staged the great feast of Xiantian 1; Ruizong attended the Anfu Gate tower to view the hundred offices' feast, continuing day into night for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: They staged the Xiantian 1 great feast again; Ruizong watched from Anfu Gate as day ran into night for over a month.

sentences.zh: 挺之上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Tingzhi memorialized remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi remonstrated as follows:

sentences.zh: 微臣竊惟陛下應天順人，發號施令，躬親大禮，昭布鴻澤，孜孜庶政，業業萬幾。

translations.literal: Your humble servant considers that Your Majesty, responding to Heaven and complying with the people, issues orders, personally performs great rites, spreads vast grace, diligently handles the myriad affairs, and is industrious in the myriad concerns.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant considers that Your Majesty, responding to Heaven and the people, issues orders, performs great rites, spreads grace, and labors over myriad affairs.

sentences.zh: 蓋以天下心為心，深戒安危之理，此誠堯、舜、禹、湯之德教也。

translations.literal: This is because you take the heart of the realm as heart and deeply guard the principle of safety and danger—this is truly the virtue and teaching of Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: You take the realm's heart as your own and guard safety and danger—truly the teaching of Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang.

sentences.zh: 奈何親禦城門，以觀大酺，累日兼夜，臣愚竊所未諭。

translations.literal: Why then personally attend the city gate to view the great feast, for days together and night as well—I, your servant, foolishly do not yet understand.
translations.idiomatic: Why then attend the city gate for the great feast day and night—I do not understand.

sentences.zh: 夫酺者，因人所利，合醵為歡，無相奪倫，不至糜弊。

translations.literal: A feast is for people's benefit, gathering contributions for joy, not overturning order, not reaching waste and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: A feast gathers contributions for joy; it should not overturn order or waste resources.

sentences.zh: 且臣卜其晝，史冊攸存，君舉必書，帝王重慎。

translations.literal: Moreover I choose the day—histories preserve it; the ruler's acts must be recorded; emperors and kings weigh heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Histories record the ruler's acts; emperors must weigh them heavily.

sentences.zh: 今乃暴衣冠於上路，羅妓樂於中宵。

translations.literal: Now you expose robes and caps on the public road and spread singing girls and music at midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Now robes and caps are exposed on the road and music spreads at midnight.

sentences.zh: 雜鄭、衛之音，縱倡優之樂。

translations.literal: You mix the sounds of Zheng and Wei and release the music of performers and jesters.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng and Wei music mingles with performers' songs.

sentences.zh: 陛下還淳復古，宵衣旰食，不矜細行，恐非聖德所宜。

translations.literal: Your Majesty returns to purity and restores antiquity, rising early and retiring late, not sparing small conduct— I fear this is not what sage virtue should be.
translations.idiomatic: You rise early and retire late to restore antiquity—such conduct ill suits sage virtue.

sentences.zh: 臣以為一不可也。

translations.literal: Your servant considers this the first impermissible thing.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first thing that must not be.

sentences.zh: 誰何警夜，伐鼓通晨，以備非常，存之善教。

translations.literal: Who patrols the night, beats drums to announce dawn, to guard against the unexpected—this good teaching is preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Night patrols and dawn drums guard against the unexpected—good teaching preserves them.

sentences.zh: 今陛下不深惟戒慎，輕違動息，重門弛禁，巨猾多徒。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty does not deeply reflect on caution and warning, lightly violates movement and rest, relaxes the heavy gates, and great villains are many.
translations.idiomatic: Now caution is lightly set aside, the gates relaxed, and villains abound.

sentences.zh: 倘有躍馬奔車，流言駭叫，一塵聽覽，有累宸衷。

translations.literal: If there were a horse leaping or carriage racing, loose talk and frightened cries reaching the imperial ear, it would burden the imperial heart.
translations.idiomatic: If horses raced or cries alarmed the throne, the imperial heart would be burdened.

sentences.zh: 臣以為二不可也。

translations.literal: Your servant considers this the second impermissible thing.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second thing that must not be.

sentences.zh: 且一人向隅，滿堂不樂；

translations.literal: Moreover when one man faces a corner, the whole hall is not merry;
translations.idiomatic: When one man faces a corner, the whole hall loses joy;

sentences.zh: 一物失所，納隍增慮。

translations.literal: when one thing loses its place, care is added to the moat.
translations.idiomatic: when one thing is out of place, care deepens.

sentences.zh: 陛下北宮多暇，西墉暫臨。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has much leisure in the Northern Palace and temporarily attends the western wall.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has leisure in the Northern Palace and attends the western wall.

sentences.zh: 青春日長，已積埃塵之弊；

translations.literal: The spring day is long and dust already accumulates in harm;
translations.idiomatic: Spring days lengthen while dust of neglect accumulates;

sentences.zh: 紫微漏永，重窮歌舞之樂。

translations.literal: the Purple Forbidden clepsydra runs long and music and dance are again exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: the palace water-clock runs long while song and dance are exhausted again.

sentences.zh: 倘令有司跛倚，下人饑倦，以陛下近猶不恤，而況於遠乎！

translations.literal: If officials limp and lean and subordinates hunger and weary, and Your Majesty nearby is still not concerned, how much more those far away!
translations.idiomatic: If officials limp and subordinates hunger while Your Majesty nearby is unconcerned, what of those far away!

sentences.zh: 聖情攸聞，豈不懍然只畏。

translations.literal: If the sacred feeling hears of it, how would you not be reverently afraid?
translations.idiomatic: If the throne heard of it, would you not be filled with dread?

sentences.zh: 臣以為三不可也。

translations.literal: Your servant considers this the third impermissible thing.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third thing that must not be.

sentences.zh: 且元正首祚，大禮頻光，百姓颙颙，咸謂業盛配天，功垂曠代。

translations.literal: Moreover at the New Year, the first blessing, great rites shine in succession; the hundred surnames look up eagerly, all saying the enterprise is grand and matches Heaven, the achievement spans an age without parallel.
translations.idiomatic: At the New Year the people look up, saying the enterprise matches Heaven and the achievement spans the age.

sentences.zh: 今陛下恩似薄於眾望，酺即過於往年。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's grace seems thinner than the multitude's hope, and the feast exceeds that of former years.
translations.idiomatic: Now grace seems thinner than hope, and the feast exceeds former years.

sentences.zh: 王公貴人，各承微旨；

translations.literal: Dukes, nobles, and great men each receive a slight intent;
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and nobles each receive a slight signal;

sentences.zh: 州縣坊曲，競為課稅。

translations.literal: prefectures, counties, wards, and lanes compete in levying taxes.
translations.idiomatic: prefectures, counties, and wards compete in levying taxes.

sentences.zh: 籲嗟道路，貿易家產，損萬人之力，營百戲之資。

translations.literal: Sighs on the roads, trading family property, damaging the strength of ten thousand men to supply the resources of a hundred entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: On the roads people sigh and trade family property, draining ten thousand men to fund a hundred shows.

sentences.zh: 適欲同其歡，而乃遺其患，復令兼夜，人何以堪？

translations.literal: You wish to share their joy yet leave them their harm; again ordering night as well—how can people bear it?
translations.idiomatic: You would share their joy yet leave them harm; ordering night as well—how can they bear it?

sentences.zh: 臣以為四不可也。

translations.literal: Your servant considers this the fourth impermissible thing.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth thing that must not be.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「罔咈百姓，以從己之欲。」

translations.literal: The Book says: "Do not oppose the hundred surnames to follow your own desires.
translations.idiomatic: The Book says, "Do not oppose the people to follow your own desires.

sentences.zh: 況自去夏霪霖，經今亢旱，農乏收成，市有騰貴。

translations.literal: Moreover since last summer's long rains and until now severe drought, farmers lack harvest and markets have soaring prices.
translations.idiomatic: Since last summer's rains and this drought, harvests fail and prices soar.

sentences.zh: 損其實，崇其虛，馳不急之務，擾方春之業。

translations.literal: Diminish the solid and exalt the empty, rush unurgent affairs, and disturb spring occupations.
translations.idiomatic: You diminish the solid for the empty, rush unurgent tasks, and disturb spring work.

sentences.zh: 前代聖主明王，忽於細微而成過患多矣，陛下可效之哉？

translations.literal: Former sage rulers and enlightened kings, neglecting the minute, became guilty of many calamities—can Your Majesty take them as models?
translations.idiomatic: Sage rulers who neglected small things brought great harm—can Your Majesty follow them?

sentences.zh: 伏望晝則歡娛，暮令休息，要令兼夜，恐無益於聖朝。

translations.literal: I beg that by day there be joy and entertainment and at evening let there be rest; if night is also required, I fear it will not benefit the sacred court.
translations.idiomatic: I beg joy by day and rest at evening; to require night as well will not benefit the court.

sentences.zh: 上納其言而止。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted his words and stopped.

sentences.zh: 時侍御史任知古恃憲威，於朝行詬詈衣冠，挺之深讓之，以為不敬，乃為臺司所劾，左遷萬州員外參軍。

translations.literal: At the time Attending Censor Ren Zhigu relied on censorial power and in the court procession reviled officials in robes and caps; Tingzhi deeply reproved him as disrespectful and was therefore impeached by the censorate and demoted Vice Administrator of Wan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Ren Zhigu reviled officials in court; Tingzhi reproved him and was impeached and demoted to Wan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開元中，為考功員外郎。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan he was Vice Director of the Evaluation Section.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan he was Vice Director of the Evaluation Section.

sentences.zh: 典舉二年，大稱平允，登科者頓減二分之一。

translations.literal: Presiding over examinations for two years, he was greatly praised as fair and even; those who passed the examination were suddenly reduced by one half.
translations.idiomatic: For two years he examined candidates with great fairness; admissions fell by half.

sentences.zh: 遷考功郎中，特敕又令知考功貢舉事，稍遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred Director of the Evaluation Section; a special edict again ordered him to know evaluation-section examination affairs, and he was gradually transferred Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He became Director of the Evaluation Section, then Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時黃門侍郎杜暹、中書侍郎李元纮同列為相，不葉。

translations.literal: At the time Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate Du Xian and Vice Minister of the Secretariat Li Yuanhong were colleagues as chief ministers and fell out.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Ministers Du Xian and Li Yuanhong were chief ministers together and fell out.

sentences.zh: 暹與挺之善，元纮素重宋遙，引為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Xian was friendly with Tingzhi; Yuanhong had long valued Song Yao and brought him in as Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was friendly with Tingzhi; Yuanhong favored Song Yao and made him Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 及與起居舍人張咺等同考吏部等第判，遙復與挺之好尚不同，遙言於元纮。

translations.literal: When with Attendant of the Diary Zhang Xuan and others he examined grades in the Ministry of Personnel, Yao again differed from Tingzhi in preference and spoke to Yuanhong.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Ministry grades with Zhang Xuan, Yao differed from Tingzhi and spoke to Yuanhong.

sentences.zh: 元纮詰譙挺之，挺之曰：「明公位尊國相，情溺小人，乃有憎惡，甚為不取也。」

translations.literal: Yuanhong reproached Tingzhi; Tingzhi said: "Your Honor, in high rank as state chief minister, emotionally drowning in petty men, yet bearing hatred—this is very unfitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhong reproached him; Tingzhi said, "You are chief minister yet dote on petty men and bear hatred—this is unfitting.

sentences.zh: 詞色俱厲。

translations.literal: His words and countenance were both severe.
translations.idiomatic: His words and bearing were severe.

sentences.zh: 元纮曰：「小人為誰？」

translations.literal: Yuanhong said: "Who is the petty man?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhong asked, "Who is the petty man?

sentences.zh: 挺之曰：「即宋遙也。」

translations.literal: Tingzhi said: "That is Song Yao."
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi said, "Song Yao."

sentences.zh: 因出為登州刺史、太原少尹。

translations.literal: He was therefore sent out Governor of Deng Prefecture and Vice Governor of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out Governor of Deng and Vice Governor of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 殿中監王毛仲使太原、朔方、幽州，計會兵馬，事隔數年，乃牒太原索器仗。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Directorate Wang Maoqi went to Taiyuan, Shuofang, and Youzhou to reckon troops and horses; the matter spanned several years before he sent a dispatch to Taiyuan demanding weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maoqi went to Taiyuan, Shuofang, and Youzhou to reckon troops; years later he demanded weapons from Taiyuan without an edict.

sentences.zh: 挺之以不挾敕，毛仲寵幸久，恐有變故，密奏之。

translations.literal: Tingzhi, because he did not carry an edict and Maoqi had long enjoyed favor, feared there might be change, and secretly memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi, seeing no edict and fearing Maoqi's long favor, secretly memorialized.

sentences.zh: 尋遷濮、汴二州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred Governor of Pu and Bian prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he governed Pu and Bian.

sentences.zh: 挺之所歷皆嚴整，吏不敢犯，及蒞大郡，人乃重足側息。

translations.literal: Wherever Tingzhi served he were stern and orderly; clerks did not dare offend; when he arrived at great prefectures people walked as if on tiptoe, holding their breath.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he was stern; clerks dared not offend; in great prefectures people trembled.

sentences.zh: 二十年，毛仲得罪賜死，玄宗思曩日之奏，擢為刑部侍郎，深見恩遇，改太府卿。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Maoqi was condemned and granted death; Emperor Xuanzong recalled the former memorial and promoted him Vice Minister of Punishments, deeply favored, and changed him Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Maoqi was put to death; the Emperor recalled Tingzhi's memorial and promoted him Vice Minister of Punishments, then Director of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 與張九齡相善，九齡入相，用挺之為尚書左丞，知吏部選，陸景融知兵部選，皆為一時精選。

translations.literal: He was friendly with Zhang Jiuling; when Jiuling entered the chancellorship he used Tingzhi as Left Assistant Chief Minister, knowing Personnel selection, and Lu Jingrong knowing War selection—both were choicest men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Friendly with Zhang Jiuling, when Jiuling became chief minister he made Tingzhi Left Assistant Chief Minister over Personnel and Lu Jingrong over War—both were choicest men.

sentences.zh: 時侍中裴耀卿、禮部尚書李林甫與九齡同在相位，九齡以詞學進，入視草翰林，又為中書令，甚承恩顧。

translations.literal: At the time Attendant-in-Chief Pei Yaoji and Minister of Rites Li Linfu were in the chief minister's post with Jiuling; Jiuling advanced through literary learning, entered to view drafts in the Hanlin, and again was Chief Minister of the Secretariat, greatly receiving favor.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yaoji and Li Linfu shared office with Jiuling, who had risen by literary learning and enjoyed great favor as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 耀卿與九齡素善，林甫巧密，知九齡方承恩遇，善事之，意未相與。

translations.literal: Yaoji and Jiuling had long been on good terms; Linfu was crafty and close, knowing Jiuling then received favor, and served him well, but in intent they were not yet allied.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoji and Jiuling were old friends; crafty Linfu served Jiuling well but was not yet allied in intent.

sentences.zh: 林甫引蕭炅為戶部侍郎，嘗與挺之同行慶吊，客次有《禮記》，蕭炅讀之曰：「蒸嘗伏獵。」

translations.literal: Linfu brought in Xiao Jiong as Vice Minister of Revenue; once when attending a condolence or congratulation with Tingzhi, in the guest place there was the Book of Rites; Xiao Jiong read: "Steaming and offering, lying in wait for the hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu brought in Xiao Jiong as Vice Minister of Revenue; at a condolence visit Jiong read from the Book of Rites, "Steaming and offering, lying in wait for the hunt.

sentences.zh: 炅早從官，無學術，不識「伏臘」之意，誤讀之。

translations.literal: Jiong had early entered office without learning and did not know the meaning of "winter and summer sacrifices"; he misread it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong had entered office young without learning and misread "winter and summer sacrifices" as "lying in wait for the hunt."

sentences.zh: 挺之戲問，炅對如初。

translations.literal: Tingzhi jested and asked; Jiong answered as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi jested and asked again; Jiong answered as before.

sentences.zh: 挺之白九齡曰：「省中豈有『伏獵侍郎。』」

translations.literal: Tingzhi told Jiuling: "In the Secretariat how can there be a 'Vice Minister who lies in wait for the hunt'?
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi told Jiuling, "How can the Secretariat harbor a 'Hunt-in-Wait Vice Minister'?

sentences.zh: 由是出為岐州刺史，林甫深恨之。

translations.literal: Because of this he was sent out Governor of Qi Prefecture, and Linfu deeply hated him.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was sent out as Governor of Qi, and Linfu deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 九齡嘗欲引挺之同居相位，謂之曰：「李尚書深承聖恩，足下宜一造門款狎。」

translations.literal: Jiuling once wished to bring Tingzhi to share the chief minister's post and told him: "Minister Li deeply receives sacred favor; you should once visit his gate and become intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling wished to share office with Tingzhi and said, "Minister Li enjoys great favor—you should visit his gate and cultivate him.

sentences.zh: 挺之素負氣，薄其為人，三年，非公事竟不私造其門，以此彌為林甫所嫉。

translations.literal: Tingzhi by nature bore proud spirit and thought little of his conduct; for three years, apart from public business he never privately visited his gate, and on this account was the more envied by Linfu.
translations.idiomatic: Proud by nature and disdainful of Linfu, for three years Tingzhi never visited him except on public business, which made Linfu hate him all the more.

sentences.zh: 及挺之囑蔚州刺史王元琰，林甫使人詰於禁中，以此九齡罷相，挺之出為洺州刺史，二十九年，移絳郡太守。

translations.literal: When Tingzhi entrusted Governor of Wei Prefecture Wang Yuanyan, Linfu had someone interrogate in the forbidden palace; because of this Jiuling left the chancellorship, Tingzhi was sent out Governor of Ming Prefecture, and in the twenty-ninth year was transferred Administrator of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingzhi entrusted Wang Yuanyan, Linfu interrogated him in the palace; Jiuling lost the chancellorship, Tingzhi was sent to Ming, and in year 29 to Jiang.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，玄宗嘗謂林甫曰：「嚴挺之何在？

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao Emperor Xuanzong once told Linfu: "Where is Yan Tingzhi?
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 the Emperor asked Linfu, "Where is Yan Tingzhi?

sentences.zh: 此人亦堪進用。」

translations.literal: This man too is fit for advancement and employment.
translations.idiomatic: This man too is fit for use.

sentences.zh: 林甫乃召其弟損之至門敘故，云「當授子員外郎」，因謂之曰：「聖人視賢兄極深，要須作一計，入城對見，當有大用。」

translations.literal: Linfu therefore summoned his younger brother Sun to the gate to speak of old times, saying "I shall appoint your son Vice Director," and therefore told him: "The Sage views your worthy elder brother very deeply; you must make a plan—enter the city for audience and there will be great employment."
translations.idiomatic: Linfu summoned Tingzhi's brother Sun, promised his son a post, and said, "The Emperor favors your brother—have him enter the city for audience and he will be greatly used."

sentences.zh: 令損之取絳郡一狀，云：「有少風氣，請入京就醫。」

translations.literal: He ordered Sun to take a petition from Jiang Prefecture saying: "There is slight wind qi; I beg to enter the capital to seek treatment."
translations.idiomatic: He had Sun take a Jiang petition saying Tingzhi had slight wind ailment and begged to enter the capital for treatment.

sentences.zh: 林甫將狀奏云：「挺之年高，近患風，且須授閑官就醫。」

translations.literal: Linfu was about to memorialize the petition saying: "Tingzhi is advanced in years, recently ill with wind, and needs an honorary post to seek treatment."
translations.idiomatic: Linfu memorialized that Tingzhi was old, recently ill with wind, and needed an honorary post for treatment.

sentences.zh: 玄宗嘆叱久之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong sighed and reproached for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sighed and reproached at length.

sentences.zh: 林甫奏授員外詹事，便令東京養疾。

translations.literal: Linfu memorialized appointing him Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household and ordered him to convalesce in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu appointed him Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household and sent him to convalesce in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 挺之素歸心釋典，事僧惠義。

translations.literal: Tingzhi had long turned his heart to Buddhist scriptures and served the monk Huiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi had long devoted himself to Buddhist scriptures and served the monk Huiyi.

sentences.zh: 及至東都，郁郁不得志，成疾。

translations.literal: When he reached the Eastern Capital he was depressed and without fulfillment of will, and fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Capital he was depressed and unfulfilled, and fell ill.

sentences.zh: 自為墓誌曰：「天寶元年，嚴挺之自絳郡太守抗疏陳乞，天恩允請，許養疾歸閑，兼授太子詹事。

translations.literal: He himself composed his tomb inscription: "In the first year of Tianbao, Yan Tingzhi, from Administrator of Jiang Prefecture, memorialized in resistance begging leave; Heaven's grace granted the request, allowing him to convalesce in retirement and concurrently appointing him Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote his own epitaph: "In Tianbao 1, Yan Tingzhi, Administrator of Jiang, memorialized for leave; Heaven granted it, allowing retirement and appointing him Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 前後歷任二十五官，每承聖恩，嘗忝獎擢，不盡驅策，駑蹇何階，仰答鴻造？

translations.literal: Formerly and later he held twenty-five offices; each time he received sacred favor he once disgraced himself with reward and promotion, not fully driven and whipped—how could a lame nag have a step to answer vast creation?
translations.idiomatic: He held twenty-five offices, each time favored yet not fully used—how could a lame nag repay such grace?

sentences.zh: 春秋七十，無所展用，為人士所悲。

translations.literal: At seventy years of the spring and autumn annals he had nothing to display and use—gentlemen grieve for it.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy he had nothing left to accomplish—men of the time grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，寢疾，終於洛陽某裏之私第。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year he lay ill and died in a private residence in a certain lane of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he fell ill and died at a private residence in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，葬於大照和尚塔次西原，禮也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was buried west of the Dazhao monk's pagoda, as ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was buried west of the Dazhao pagoda, as ritual required.

sentences.zh: 盡忠事君，叨載國史，勉拙從仕，或布人謠。

translations.literal: Serving the ruler with full loyalty, I am recorded in the state history; striving in blunt service from office, sometimes spreading among the people in song.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal in service, recorded in state history; striving in office, sometimes praised in popular song.

sentences.zh: 陵谷可以自紀，文章焉用為飾。

translations.literal: Hills and valleys can record themselves; of what use is literary ornament?
translations.idiomatic: Hills and valleys record themselves—what need of literary ornament?

sentences.zh: 遺文薄葬，斂以時服。」

translations.literal: Leaving writings, thin burial, enshrouded in timely garments.
translations.idiomatic: He left writings, asked for a simple burial, and was enshrouded in ordinary garments.

sentences.zh: 挺之與裴寬皆奉佛。

translations.literal: Tingzhi and Pei Kuan both practiced Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi and Pei Kuan both followed Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 開元末，惠義卒，挺之服缞麻送於龕所。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyuan Huiyi died; Tingzhi wore hemp mourning and escorted to the niche place.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Kaiyuan, when Huiyi died, Tingzhi wore hemp mourning to the niche.

sentences.zh: 寬為河南尹，僧普寂卒，寬與妻子皆服缞绖，設次哭臨，妻子送喪至嵩山。

translations.literal: Kuan was Metropolitan Governor of Henan; when the monk Puji died, Kuan and his wife and children all wore hemp and hemp headbands, set up a mourning station and wailed, and the wife and children escorted the funeral to Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan, as Metropolitan Governor of Henan, when Puji died wore mourning with wife and children, wailed at a mourning station, and sent them to escort the funeral to Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 故挺之誌文云「葬於大照塔側」，祈其靈祐也。

translations.literal: Therefore Tingzhi's epitaph says "buried beside the Dazhao pagoda," praying for spiritual blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the epitaph says "buried beside the Dazhao pagoda," praying for the monk's blessing.

sentences.zh: 挺之素重交結，有許與，凡舊交先歿者，厚撫其妻子，凡嫁孤女數十人，時人重之。

translations.literal: Tingzhi by nature greatly valued forming bonds; he had promises; for every old friend who died first he generously supported wife and children, and in all married off orphaned daughters numbering several tens—people of the time thought much of him.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi valued friendship; he generously supported the families of dead friends and married off dozens of orphaned daughters—contemporaries esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 子武，廣德中黃門侍郎、成都尹、劍南節度使。

translations.literal: His son Wu, in the Guangde era, was Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate, Metropolitan Governor of Chengdu, and Military Commissioner of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wu, in Guangde, was Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate, Governor of Chengdu, and Military Commissioner of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：崔日用附會三思，以取高位，預討韋氏，遂握重權。

translations.literal: The historian says: Cui Riyong attached himself to Sansi to gain high rank, took part in suppressing the Wei faction, and then grasped heavy power.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Cui Riyong joined Sansi to rise high, helped suppress the Wei faction, and grasped heavy power.

sentences.zh: 自言「吾一生行事，皆臨時制變，不必專守始謀」，信矣。

translations.literal: He himself said "In all my life's actions I adapt on the spot and need not cling to the original plan"—how true.
translations.idiomatic: His saying that he adapted on the spot and need not cling to the original plan was indeed true.

sentences.zh: 與夫守死善道者，不可同年而語也。

translations.literal: Compared with those who hold to death and preserve the Way, he cannot be spoken of in the same year.
translations.idiomatic: He cannot be compared with those who hold to death and preserve the Way.

sentences.zh: 張嘉貞雖不立田園，奈急於勢利，朋比近習，杖姜皎、伷先，非中立之士也。

translations.literal: Although Zhang Jiazhen did not establish estates, he was impatient for power and profit, formed factions with near intimates, and beat Jiang Jiao and Xianxian—he was not a man of the middle and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiazhen established no estates, yet he craved power, formed factions, and had Jiang Jiao and Xianxian beaten—he was no impartial man.

sentences.zh: 蕭嵩位極中令，異政無聞，樹破虜之勛，真致遠之器。

translations.literal: Xiao Song reached the utmost as Chief Minister; no unusual government was heard of, yet he built merit in breaking the barbarians—truly an instrument for reaching far.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Song reached the chief ministership without notable policy, yet broke the barbarians—truly a man who could go far.

sentences.zh: 九齡文學政事，咸有所稱，一時之選也。

translations.literal: Jiuling in literary learning and government affairs was praised in both— a choice man of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling was praised in both letters and government—a choice man of his age.

sentences.zh: 適之臨下雖簡，在公克勤，惜乎不得其死也！

translations.literal: Shizhi, though easy with subordinates, was diligent in public affairs—alas that he did not die a natural death!
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi was easy below yet diligent in office—alas that he did not die naturally!

sentences.zh: 挺之才略器識，不下諸公，恥近權門，為人所惡，不登臺輔，養疾宮僚。

translations.literal: Tingzhi's talent, plan, and discernment were not below the dukes and ministers; he was ashamed to approach power's gate, was hated by men, did not ascend the terrace and assistant post, and convalesced as a palace official.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi's talent was not below his peers; shunning power's gate, he was hated, never reached the chancellorship, and ended convalescing as a palace official.

sentences.zh: 雖富貴在天，窮達有命，彼林甫者，誠可投畀豺虎也。

translations.literal: Although wealth and nobility lie with Heaven and success and failure have mandate, that Linfu—truly he may be cast to wolves and tigers.
translations.idiomatic: Though fortune is Heaven's and fate Heaven's, that Linfu might truly be cast to wolves and tigers.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：開元之代，多士盈庭。

translations.literal: The encomium says: In the Kaiyuan era, gentlemen filled the court.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: In the Kaiyuan era the court was full of talent.

sentences.zh: 日用無守，嘉貞近名。

translations.literal: Riyong had no constancy; Jiazhen neared fame.
translations.idiomatic: Riyong lacked constancy; Jiazhen courted fame.

sentences.zh: 嵩、齡、適、挺，各有度程。

translations.literal: Song, Jiuling, Shizhi, and Tingzhi each had his measure.
translations.idiomatic: Song, Jiuling, Shizhi, and Tingzhi each had his measure.

sentences.zh: 大位俱極，半慚德馨。

translations.literal: All reached the great post, yet half ashamed at the fragrance of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: All reached the summit of rank, yet half fell short of true virtue.
